## See what is installed, and what the app loaded

`doctor` checks one folder you name. The question that actually gets asked is
"why is my plugin not in the sidebar?", and the answer needs three things at once:
what is installed, whether each installed copy is valid, and which of them the
running app actually loaded.

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
dsh-aiignore           0.37.1    loaded       ok
demo-panel             0.3.0     not loaded   ok  — dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json does not list it, and the loader mounts only listed bundles
                                            fix: add "demo-panel" to dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json (or run `dsh plugin add demo-panel`), then restart the app

1 installed plugin(s) are not in the running app:
```

"Not loaded" has three different causes, and `audit` names the one that applies
instead of offering a blanket restart:

- **Not in `dsh.profile.bundles`.** `pnpm add` (or `npm install`) installs the
  package but does not tell the loader to mount it. Add the package name to
  `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`, or run
  `dsh plugin add <name>`, then restart the app.
- **No `dsh.bundle`.** The package declares `dsh` but no patch file to mount.
  Add `dsh.bundle.patch` to its `package.json` and ship the patch file, then
  reinstall.
- **Listed, but the app predates the install.** The profile is already correct;
  restart the app once to read the new list.

Advisories (`engines.dsh`, README Requirements) are counted apart from problems:
the market index needs them, the loader does not, so they should not bury a plugin
that is actually broken.

`audit` exits `1` when an installed plugin has a hard failure **or** when the
running app did not load at least one installed plugin, so CI can gate on a
profile where the app silently skipped a plugin. It exits `0` when every
installed plugin is loaded and valid. When `--host` is given but the app cannot
be reached, the command has not observed the graph it was asked for: it prints
the `/plugins/events` URL it could not read, prints no plugin rows or clean
summary, and exits `2` so a CI gate cannot pass against an unreachable app.
Without `--host`, the loaded column is `?` and only hard failures change the
exit code.

`audit --home <dir>` scans a different profile home; both `~/.dsh` and
`~\.dsh` expand. A bare `--home`, or one followed by another flag such as
`--timeout 50` or `--json`, is a missing value rather than a request to scan
`$HOME/.dsh` or a folder literally named after the flag: the command exits `2`,
names `--home`, and prints no profile report. An explicit `--home` must be an
existing directory: a missing path, a regular file and a dangling symlink each
exit `2` naming `--home` and the resolved path, instead of printing "no plugins
installed in any profile" for a home the audit never read. An existing empty
directory still exits `0` with that line, and omitting `--home` still scans the
default `~/.dsh`.

Without `--host` the loaded column is `?`, because guessing would be worse than
saying nothing. Only packages that declare a `dsh` field, plus packages the
profile names in `dsh.profile.bundles`, are audited — the rest of `node_modules`
is ordinary dependencies, and auditing those is noise.

An installed package whose `package.json` cannot be read is the exception: the
`dsh` field that would mark it as a plugin is in the file that failed to parse.
If its name is still in `dsh.profile.bundles`, `audit` reports a `manifest`
failure naming the unreadable `package.json` and exits `1` instead of treating
the folder as an ordinary dependency. A truncated manifest from an interrupted
install therefore cannot make the plugin disappear from the report, and a valid
sibling plugin is still listed on the same run. The exception stays narrow: a
damaged `package.json` in a package that is neither in `dsh.profile.bundles` nor
readable enough to expose a `dsh` field is still an ordinary dependency and is
skipped, so one broken transitive install does not fail every audit.

The profile file gets the same treatment. If
`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json` is truncated or is not a JSON object,
`audit` prints an `unreadable profile` row with a `profile manifest` failure
naming the file and the parse error, and exits `1`. It does not quietly treat
the profile as one that declares no bundles, so a damaged profile cannot hide
the plugin it declares behind "no plugins installed in any profile". Any valid
plugin still installed in that profile is listed beside the profile finding.

A declared bundle can also parse but carry no `dsh` field at all. The profile
says the loader will mount it, so `audit` prints a `no dsh field` row with a
`dsh field` failure naming the declaring `package.json` and exits `1`, instead
of skipping the package and reporting the profile as having no plugins. The
skip still applies to a package that is not in `dsh.profile.bundles`; a profile
containing only ordinary dependencies prints no plugin rows and exits `0`.

A declared bundle can also be missing entirely. If a name stays in
`dsh.profile.bundles` after its `node_modules/<name>` folder is removed (an
interrupted install, or a package deleted by hand), `audit` prints a `missing`
row with an `install` failure naming the absent folder and exits `1`, while
still listing the healthy plugins on the same run. An absent package that the
profile never declared is not an install record, so it is not invented in the
report; a regression test removes the name from the profile and requires the
shipped CLI to exit `0` without printing it.

## Edit a plugin that is already installed

The host already swaps a rebuilt bundle without a page reload: it watches each plugin's entry artifact and reports a `rebuilt` frame on `/plugins/events`. `dev` puts the new file where the host is looking, then **proves** the frame arrived instead of asking you to check by eye.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

![dsh-plugin dev printing the revision the app reported](docs/dev.gif)

*Recorded from a real run against the running app: the last line is the revision the app sent back on `/plugins/events`, not a message the tool printed on faith.*

```
demo-aiignore: /work/plugin/client.js -> ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-aiignore/client.js
initial: copied 163647 bytes at 1:18:43 AM
reloaded dsh-aiignore (rev e0c0230c4fc9)
watching /work/plugin
```

That last line is the whole point: the revision came back from the app's own event stream, so "it reloaded" is a fact, not a hope.

A plugin the running app never loaded cannot be reloaded, and the app says so by leaving it out of the graph it sends first. `dev` reads that graph, so a freshly installed plugin gets the sentence that fixes it instead of a timeout:

```
copied, but not confirmed: the running app has not loaded demo-panel, so it will not report a reload; restart the app once after installing it
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dest <dir>` | write into this installed copy instead of searching `~/.dsh/profiles/*/node_modules/<name>` |
| `--entry <file>` | copy this file instead of `dsh.client.entry`, `client.js`, `lib/client.js` |
| `--build <command>` | run this before each copy (a failed build copies nothing) |
| `--host <url>` | confirm the reload against the app at this URL; without it the copy still happens and the tool says it is unconfirmed |
| `--once` | copy once and exit, for scripts |

Two things it does not do, because the host does not: React state inside the reloaded plugin is lost, and a failed swap does not roll back to the previous bundle.

## Use it in CI

The same checks run as a GitHub Action, so a tag cannot go out on a plugin that would not install:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit@v1
  with:
    dir: plugin        # the folder holding the plugin's package.json
    command: verify    # pack it, install the tarball, mount the panel
```

`verify` is the default because it is the only check that reads what a user
actually installs: `doctor` reads the working copy, so a `files` list that
forgets `client.js` passes it and fails only after `npm i`.

`command: doctor` stops at the manifest checks (fast, no install), and
`command: index` audits `market/index.json` instead, failing on any version whose
`engines.dsh` is missing or is not a semver range (a malformed value such as
`>=banana`, or a single pinned version such as `0.2.0`, both fail). It also
rejects an index it cannot audit: a missing `plugins` or `versions` array, a
plugin entry without a name, two entries sharing one name, a version entry
without `version`, and a non-SemVer `version`. Each failure names the file and
the plugin, entry, or both duplicate positions. A duplicate is rejected before
any audit, so the second entry cannot inherit the first entry's clean result or
produce an `ok` line.
Pin `version:` if you would rather not track the latest release.

## Check a plugin you have not cloned

The panel takes three kinds of input: a folder, `owner/repo`, or a GitHub URL.
A bare name is a search, not a guess — it asks GitHub, lists the matches with
their stars, and checks the one you pick. A repository is downloaded once as a
tarball into a temp folder, so nothing is cloned into your workspace and
nothing is installed.

The CLI reads a repository straight from the GitHub API:

```bash
dsh-plugin doctor --remote V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
```

```text
dsh-plugin doctor: 1 problem(s) in V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
  ⨯ engines.dsh: engines.dsh is missing, so a host that enforces the range rejects the install as "incompatible with dsh"; declare the range you support, e.g. "engines": { "dsh": ">=0.2.0" }
```

That is the whole reason this mode exists: the plugin hub files failed installs
back into plugin repositories, and the report is a sentence — `plugin install
failed`, `plugin does not support the DSH version in use` — that never names a
file. Reading `package.json` over the API is enough to name it.

What it can see, and what it cannot:

- Manifest checks (`engines.dsh`, `dsh field`, `files`, `dsh.client`,
  `exports`) run on the real `package.json`.
- README checks (`readme`) run on the text GitHub serves: the README must have
  a `Requirements` heading and must state the host range `package.json`
  declares. A repository whose checkout fails `readme` fails the remote check
  too, with the same sentence.
- File checks (does `exports["./client"]` point at a file that exists, does the
  root export `apply`) need the tree. npm runs `prepack` and `prepare` before
  `npm pack` creates the tarball, and `prepublishOnly` before `npm publish`
  does, so a package whose lifecycle hook builds those files publishes files it
  does not commit: those checks are **skipped with a note** instead of calling a
  working plugin broken. A plain `build` script is not a lifecycle hook and is
  not evidence by itself, because npm never runs it unless `prepack` or
  `prepare` calls it; put the build there if it produces shipped files.
- Public repositories work anonymously, but GitHub allows 60 requests an hour.
  Export `GH_TOKEN` (or `GITHUB_TOKEN`) to audit more than one or two.

To check a whole list in one pass, put one `owner/repo` per line in a file and
pass it with `--from` (`-` reads standard input):

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt
```

Repositories are read four at a time by default. `--jobs N` changes that width;
values above `8` are capped at `8`, and `--jobs 1` walks the list one repository
at a time, the timing the command had before batching. The output — and the
`--json` array — still follows the input list, and every verdict is the one the
sequential run produced, so a diff between two runs compares repositories rather
than scheduling.

When GitHub answers `403` or `429`, the shared quota is gone, so the batch stops
starting new repositories and marks every entry it could not read as
`rate-limited` instead of `clean` or `unreadable`. If the response carries
`x-ratelimit-reset` (or `retry-after`), the reset time is printed with the
verdict, and the remaining entries are reported without another request.

# readme-bom-no-heading-fixture

Requires dsh >=0.2.0.

# dsh-plugin-toolkit

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dw/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
[![CI](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](LICENSE)


![dsh-plugin-toolkit](docs/card.png)

English · [中文](./README.zh.md)

Everything a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin needs between `init` and a version the market index accepts: scaffolding, a test harness for the client bundle, a way to see a change without restarting the app, and a release that does not depend on remembering fourteen steps.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel   # a plugin that already passes the checks
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest verify .                          # pack it, install the tarball, mount the panel
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest release --pr --merge              # tag, wait for npm, update the index, open and merge the PR
```

## The panel

![The Plugin doctor tab, on a plugin that fails two checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/panel.png)

The same checks, in the right sidebar: type a folder, an `owner/repo`, or a GitHub link, and it says which one would fail and why. Nothing is installed and nothing is written.

## Three paths

| You are… | Start with | Then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| writing your first plugin | [`init`](#1-write-a-plugin) | `doctor`, `fix`, `verify` |
| changing a panel that is already installed | [`dev`](#2-develop-a-panel) | `mount`, the testkit, `audit` |
| shipping a version | [`verify`](#3-ship-a-version) | `release`, `index` |

It also installs as a plugin. `dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-toolkit` puts a
**插件体检 / Plugin doctor** panel under the conversation and a tab in the right
sidebar. Give it a folder that holds a plugin's `package.json`, or just
`owner/repo` — or a repository name, which it searches GitHub for and lists the
candidates to pick from. It then runs the same checks `verify` runs and says
which one would break the install, with the reason on the line — the same
answers as the CLI, without leaving the app.

```
$ dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-toolkit
```

### 1. Write a plugin

[`init`](#start-from-a-plugin-that-already-passes) writes the files whose absence shows up as a failed first publish — `engines.dsh`, the patch file, a `files` list that ships the code, a client bundle, a test for it, and the CI that runs both. `doctor` then checks the same things without writing anything, and [`verify`](#prove-the-tarball-works-not-just-the-repository) checks the tarball instead of the working copy.

If a plugin already exists, `doctor --fix` turns the failing checks into a
repair plan. It names the file and the edit for every problem, writes nothing
until you add `--write`, and then runs the checks again. `fix --engines` is
still there when the host range is the only thing you need to change.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel
cd my-panel && npm install && npm test && npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest doctor .
```

### 2. Develop a panel

A plugin's client code is one file that calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({factory})` — there is no module to import, so the usual React test setup does not apply. [`testkit`](#test-a-panel-without-a-browser) supplies the missing half, and [`dev`](#edit-a-plugin-that-is-already-installed) pushes a rebuilt bundle into the running app.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest mount ./client.js     # what a user would see, without the app
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

### 3. Ship a version

`verify` first (it is the only check that reads the tarball), then `release`, which tags, waits for the registry, writes the index entry with the publish time the registry reports, and — with `--pr --merge` — opens and merges the pull request.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest verify .
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest release . --pr --merge
```

## What `verify` actually does

![Five steps, and the failure each one catches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/pipeline.svg)

The order matters. Packing first — exactly once — means the check reads the file list from the tarball `verify` installs, not from the folder you have. A separate dry run would execute `prepack` a second time, and that second execution can see a tree the first one changed, so the archive could differ from the list that was checked. Installing the tarball means the root is imported by its bare specifier — the package name the loader uses — not by a file path taken from `main` or `exports["."]`. Node ignores `main` once `exports` exists, so a package whose `exports` map has no `"."` entry fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` at that step even though the file is present. Mounting means the client bundle is actually executed, in jsdom, with a host that records what it registered. Packing first also means a panel built by a `prepack` hook exists when the source checks run: the hook has written it into the folder before `doctor`'s file checks are asked again. A hook is free to print while it builds — npm writes that output to stdout ahead of its `--json` document — so `verify` finds the tarball answer in the stream instead of assuming the whole of stdout is JSON.

Each step exists because a plugin once got past the step before it and still installed into nothing.

## Why this exists

Releasing one plugin fifteen times taught me three things the ecosystem's tooling does not cover:

1. **A version is not shipped when npm accepts it.** Registry propagation took two to eight minutes every time. `npm view` answered from a stale local cache, so I repeatedly believed a release had failed when it had not — and once believed it had succeeded when the market still could not see it.
2. **The market index is a second release, done by hand.** Each version needs an entry carrying `publishTimestamp` from the registry and `engines.dsh` from the manifest. Forget the range and the index validator rejects the PR with `Engines mismatch` — after the tag is already public.
3. **Reading a manifest is not the same as checking it.** A plugin can have a valid `package.json` and still be uninstallable: `files` that omit the entry the manifest points at, a bundle patch that does not exist, a README that never states the host range it declares.

The five failures behind these checks — a red dot with no panel, a row the host drops, an app that disables every plugin after one unguarded `apply()`, a tab nothing can open, and a checker that was wrong — are written up with their exact error text and how to reproduce each one: [Five plugins that installed and did nothing](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/blob/main/docs/why-it-exists.md).

### Four ways a plugin installs and still does nothing

Each of these shipped in a real version of this toolkit before the check below existed. A manifest check passes on all four.

| What you see | What it was | Caught by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The tab is a red dot and the panel never opens | `exports["."]` pointed at the CLI, so the loader's row had no plugin to apply | `root export` |
| The plugin is installed, the app never serves it | `dsh.client` declared, `exports["./client"]` missing — the host drops the row | `client declaration` |
| The app says the third-party plugin is unsupported and disables all of them | `apply()` read `ctx.webServer` without declaring it; cordis throws instead of returning `undefined` | `verify` (calls `apply` on a context that has no services) |
| The tab registers, and nothing in the UI opens it | `sidebarRightTabs.register()` registers a *type*; the sidebar lists what `tabs.guide()` returns | a testkit test, not `doctor` |

The first three are static: `doctor` and `verify` catch them without the app running. The fourth is a UI contract, so it needs the panel mounted and the registration inspected — that is what [`testkit`](#test-a-panel-without-a-browser) is for.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or newer (the registry is read with `fetch`; no runtime dependencies)
- Git and `gh` on `PATH` for the steps that touch GitHub
- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.0` — the version whose market index carries `engines.dsh`, which is what makes the range check meaningful
- For `testkit`: `jsdom`, `react` and `react-dom` as dev dependencies (`npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom`)

## Start from a plugin that already passes

```sh
$ npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel --title "My panel"
created 8 file(s) in /Users/you/my-panel
  .github/workflows/ci.yml
  .gitignore
  README.md
  client.js
  cordis.patch.yml
  index.js
  package.json
  test/panel.test.mjs

next: npm install && npm test && npm run doctor
```

What you get is not a snippet: it is a plugin whose `doctor` already passes (`engines.dsh`, the patch file, the `files` list), with a client bundle that registers a sidebar tab, a testkit test for it, and a CI workflow that runs both. `init` refuses a directory that is not empty unless you pass `--force`, a name npm would refuse, and a blank `--title` (pass one, such as `--title "My panel"`) — mistakes that cost the most time later.

Every command that takes a path expands a leading `~` before touching the filesystem. The tool, not the shell, expands `~` for these arguments: `cmd` and PowerShell pass `"~/my-panel"` through literally, while a POSIX shell usually expands it first. `init '~/my-panel' --name my-panel` writes into your home directory (the same files `init ~/my-panel` writes on a POSIX shell), and `doctor '~/my-panel'` reads it back. The Windows spelling `~\my-panel` works too; a directory literally named `~` is never created.

## Where it lives

The checker is docked **under the conversation**, above the input bar: a single
row, collapsed by default. Open it and it carries the whole guide — who it is
for, how to use it, what each check means, and what it cannot tell you — plus
the folder field and the results. The same panel is also a **Plugin doctor** tab
in the right sidebar, for when the conversation is busy.

The panel speaks both languages and opens in Chinese; the 中文 / EN switch sits
in the dock's header row (and in the sidebar tab) and the choice is remembered.

Look at it without the app. The preview mounts the panel with the testkit, so it
needs the optional peers; install them once with
`npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom`:

```sh
node scripts/preview.mjs /tmp/panel.html   # collapsed, open, with a result, and the tab
```

## Test a panel without a browser

A plugin's client code is one file that calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({factory})` — there is no module to import, so the usual React test setup does not apply. `testkit` supplies the missing half: a DOM, the real React, and a host context that records what the panel registers.

```sh
npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom
```

```js
import { mountClient, createFetch } from 'dsh-plugin-toolkit/testkit';

const panel = await mountClient({
  file: 'client.js',
  copy: { 'my-plugin': { title: 'My panel' } },
  fetch: createFetch({
    '/my-plugin/report': { body: { score: 71, noise: 3 } },
    '/my-plugin/apply': () => ({ status: 201, body: { score: 92 } }),
  }),
});

await panel.click('[data-testid="optimize"]');
console.assert(panel.text().includes('92'), 'the score on screen did not move');
console.assert(panel.must('[role="status"]').textContent.includes('92'));
await panel.unmount();
```

`unmount()` is async: it lets React finish the work its own unmount schedules before the DOM goes away. Skipping the `await` surfaces as `ReferenceError: window is not defined` *after* the test has already passed, which is a confusing way to learn it.

What you get back: `text()`, `html()`, `query(selector)`, `must(selector)` (throws with the rendered HTML when it misses), `click(selector)`, `type(selector, value)`, `press(selector, key)`, `focus`, `attributes(selector)`, `snapshot(dir, name)` for a normalised DOM baseline, and `host` for assertions about what the bundle registered.

### Keep a visual baseline

The DOM is the baseline: normalising class order and whitespace gives a file that fails for the reasons a screenshot would — a lost label, a control that stopped rendering — and can be reviewed in a diff instead of by eye.

```js
import { expectSnapshot } from 'dsh-plugin-toolkit/testkit';

const panel = await mountClient({ file: 'client.js' });
expectSnapshot(panel.html(), '__snapshots__', 'panel');   // throws with the element that moved
await panel.unmount();
```

First run writes nothing: it tells you to re-run with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`, so a baseline is always a decision, never a side effect. That rerun writes the normalised HTML and returns `{ status: 'written' }`; later runs return `same` or fail with the element that moved.

### Check what assistive tech sees

```js
panel.expectAria('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"]', { label: 'Protection', selected: 'true' });
assert.match(panel.must('[role="status"]').textContent, /Score moved 71 → 77/);
```

`expectAria()` compares the attributes a screen reader actually reads — `role`,
`label`, `live`, `selected`, `expanded`, `checked`, `pressed`, `disabled` — and
names the one that differs:

```
[aria-live="polite"]: expected aria text to be "9", but it is "0"
```

A missing attribute is reported as `nothing`, not as an empty string, because
those are different bugs. `panel.aria(selector)` returns the same object when you
want to assert on it yourself.

`must()` throws with the rendered markup when the selector misses, which is the difference between "the assertion failed" and "here is what the user actually got".

Every example below is shipped in the package, run by CI, and the output shown is the output it prints:

| Example | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `node examples/mount-a-bundle.mjs` | mount a real bundle, read the text, click, read it again |
| `node examples/route-stubs.mjs` | answer the routes a panel asks for, and assert on the requests |
| `node examples/baseline.mjs` | a DOM baseline compared on every run |
| `node examples/aria.mjs` | what assistive tech sees |

```sh
$ node examples/mount-a-bundle.mjs
Demo panel Count 0 0
Demo panel Count 1 1
```

```sh
$ node examples/route-stubs.mjs
Score 71
asked for: 1 route(s), undeclared route answers 404
```

To look at a bundle by hand:

```sh
npx dsh-plugin mount ./client.js            # print the text a user would see
npx dsh-plugin mount ./client.js --html     # print the markup
```

That is how the AIignore panel was checked before release: the real bundle, mounted in Node, against a stubbed `/aiignore/*`:

```
$ npx dsh-plugin mount ../ai-context-doctor/plugin/client.js
AIignore No workspace yet Could not read the report …
```

## Put the badge on a plugin that passes

If `verify` passes on your plugin, this badge says so and links back here:

```md
[![checked with dsh-plugin-toolkit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
```

It is a claim, not a decoration: add it only when `dsh-plugin verify .` exits 0.

## Start from the example

[`dsh-plugin-example`](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-example) is a ~70-line plugin: one sidebar tab, two languages, one behaviour test, CI that runs `verify` through the composite action. It is the shape this toolkit expects, so it is also the fastest way to see whether the toolkit fits your plugin. It is a GitHub template too: **Use this template** starts you on a plugin whose first publish already passes.

```sh
dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-example
```

## See what is installed, and what the app loaded

`doctor` checks one folder you name. The question that actually gets asked is
"why is my plugin not in the sidebar?", and the answer needs three things at once:
what is installed, whether each installed copy is valid, and which of them the
running app actually loaded.

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
dsh-aiignore           0.37.1    loaded       ok
demo-panel             0.3.0     not loaded   ok  — dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json does not list it, and the loader mounts only listed bundles
                                            fix: add "demo-panel" to dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json (or run `dsh plugin add demo-panel`), then restart the app

1 installed plugin(s) are not in the running app:
```

"Not loaded" has three different causes, and `audit` names the one that applies
instead of offering a blanket restart:

- **Not in `dsh.profile.bundles`.** `pnpm add` (or `npm install`) installs the
  package but does not tell the loader to mount it. Add the package name to
  `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`, or run
  `dsh plugin add <name>`, then restart the app.
- **No `dsh.bundle`.** The package declares `dsh` but no patch file to mount.
  Add `dsh.bundle.patch` to its `package.json` and ship the patch file, then
  reinstall.
- **Listed, but the app predates the install.** The profile is already correct;
  restart the app once to read the new list.

Advisories (`engines.dsh`, README Requirements) are counted apart from problems:
the market index needs them, the loader does not, so they should not bury a plugin
that is actually broken.

`audit` exits `1` when an installed plugin has a hard failure **or** when the
running app did not load at least one installed plugin, so CI can gate on a
profile where the app silently skipped a plugin. It exits `0` when every
installed plugin is loaded and valid. When `--host` is given but the app cannot
be reached, the command has not observed the graph it was asked for: it prints
the `/plugins/events` URL it could not read, prints no plugin rows or clean
summary, and exits `2` so a CI gate cannot pass against an unreachable app.
Without `--host`, the loaded column is `?` and only hard failures change the
exit code.

`audit --home <dir>` scans a different profile home; both `~/.dsh` and
`~\.dsh` expand. A bare `--home`, or one followed by another flag such as
`--timeout 50` or `--json`, is a missing value rather than a request to scan
`$HOME/.dsh` or a folder literally named after the flag: the command exits `2`,
names `--home`, and prints no profile report. An explicit `--home` must be an
existing directory: a missing path, a regular file and a dangling symlink each
exit `2` naming `--home` and the resolved path, instead of printing "no plugins
installed in any profile" for a home the audit never read. An existing empty
directory still exits `0` with that line, and omitting `--home` still scans the
default `~/.dsh`.

Without `--host` the loaded column is `?`, because guessing would be worse than
saying nothing. Only packages that declare a `dsh` field, plus packages the
profile names in `dsh.profile.bundles`, are audited — the rest of `node_modules`
is ordinary dependencies, and auditing those is noise.

An installed package whose `package.json` cannot be read is the exception: the
`dsh` field that would mark it as a plugin is in the file that failed to parse.
If its name is still in `dsh.profile.bundles`, `audit` reports a `manifest`
failure naming the unreadable `package.json` and exits `1` instead of treating
the folder as an ordinary dependency. A truncated manifest from an interrupted
install therefore cannot make the plugin disappear from the report, and a valid
sibling plugin is still listed on the same run. The exception stays narrow: a
damaged `package.json` in a package that is neither in `dsh.profile.bundles` nor
readable enough to expose a `dsh` field is still an ordinary dependency and is
skipped, so one broken transitive install does not fail every audit.

The profile file gets the same treatment. If
`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json` is truncated or is not a JSON object,
`audit` prints an `unreadable profile` row with a `profile manifest` failure
naming the file and the parse error, and exits `1`. It does not quietly treat
the profile as one that declares no bundles, so a damaged profile cannot hide
the plugin it declares behind "no plugins installed in any profile". Any valid
plugin still installed in that profile is listed beside the profile finding.

A declared bundle can also parse but carry no `dsh` field at all. The profile
says the loader will mount it, so `audit` prints a `no dsh field` row with a
`dsh field` failure naming the declaring `package.json` and exits `1`, instead
of skipping the package and reporting the profile as having no plugins. The
skip still applies to a package that is not in `dsh.profile.bundles`; a profile
containing only ordinary dependencies prints no plugin rows and exits `0`.

A declared bundle can also be missing entirely. If a name stays in
`dsh.profile.bundles` after its `node_modules/<name>` folder is removed (an
interrupted install, or a package deleted by hand), `audit` prints a `missing`
row with an `install` failure naming the absent folder and exits `1`, while
still listing the healthy plugins on the same run. An absent package that the
profile never declared is not an install record, so it is not invented in the
report; a regression test removes the name from the profile and requires the
shipped CLI to exit `0` without printing it.

## Edit a plugin that is already installed

The host already swaps a rebuilt bundle without a page reload: it watches each plugin's entry artifact and reports a `rebuilt` frame on `/plugins/events`. `dev` puts the new file where the host is looking, then **proves** the frame arrived instead of asking you to check by eye.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

![dsh-plugin dev printing the revision the app reported](docs/dev.gif)

*Recorded from a real run against the running app: the last line is the revision the app sent back on `/plugins/events`, not a message the tool printed on faith.*

```
demo-aiignore: /work/plugin/client.js -> ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-aiignore/client.js
initial: copied 163647 bytes at 1:18:43 AM
reloaded dsh-aiignore (rev e0c0230c4fc9)
watching /work/plugin
```

That last line is the whole point: the revision came back from the app's own event stream, so "it reloaded" is a fact, not a hope.

A plugin the running app never loaded cannot be reloaded, and the app says so by leaving it out of the graph it sends first. `dev` reads that graph, so a freshly installed plugin gets the sentence that fixes it instead of a timeout:

```
copied, but not confirmed: the running app has not loaded demo-panel, so it will not report a reload; restart the app once after installing it
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dest <dir>` | write into this installed copy instead of searching `~/.dsh/profiles/*/node_modules/<name>` |
| `--entry <file>` | copy this file instead of `dsh.client.entry`, `client.js`, `lib/client.js` |
| `--build <command>` | run this before each copy (a failed build copies nothing) |
| `--host <url>` | confirm the reload against the app at this URL; without it the copy still happens and the tool says it is unconfirmed |
| `--once` | copy once and exit, for scripts |

Two things it does not do, because the host does not: React state inside the reloaded plugin is lost, and a failed swap does not roll back to the previous bundle.

## Use it in CI

The same checks run as a GitHub Action, so a tag cannot go out on a plugin that would not install:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit@v1
  with:
    dir: plugin        # the folder holding the plugin's package.json
    command: verify    # pack it, install the tarball, mount the panel
```

`verify` is the default because it is the only check that reads what a user
actually installs: `doctor` reads the working copy, so a `files` list that
forgets `client.js` passes it and fails only after `npm i`.

`command: doctor` stops at the manifest checks (fast, no install), and
`command: index` audits `market/index.json` instead, failing on any version whose
`engines.dsh` is missing or is not a semver range (a malformed value such as
`>=banana`, or a single pinned version such as `0.2.0`, both fail). It also
rejects an index it cannot audit: a missing `plugins` or `versions` array, a
plugin entry without a name, two entries sharing one name, a version entry
without `version`, and a non-SemVer `version`. Each failure names the file and
the plugin, entry, or both duplicate positions. A duplicate is rejected before
any audit, so the second entry cannot inherit the first entry's clean result or
produce an `ok` line.
Pin `version:` if you would rather not track the latest release.

## Check a plugin you have not cloned

The panel takes three kinds of input: a folder, `owner/repo`, or a GitHub URL.
A bare name is a search, not a guess — it asks GitHub, lists the matches with
their stars, and checks the one you pick. A repository is downloaded once as a
tarball into a temp folder, so nothing is cloned into your workspace and
nothing is installed.

The CLI reads a repository straight from the GitHub API:

```bash
dsh-plugin doctor --remote V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
```

```text
dsh-plugin doctor: 1 problem(s) in V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
  ⨯ engines.dsh: engines.dsh is missing, so a host that enforces the range rejects the install as "incompatible with dsh"; declare the range you support, e.g. "engines": { "dsh": ">=0.2.0" }
```

That is the whole reason this mode exists: the plugin hub files failed installs
back into plugin repositories, and the report is a sentence — `plugin install
failed`, `plugin does not support the DSH version in use` — that never names a
file. Reading `package.json` over the API is enough to name it.

What it can see, and what it cannot:

- Manifest checks (`engines.dsh`, `dsh field`, `files`, `dsh.client`,
  `exports`) run on the real `package.json`.
- README checks (`readme`) run on the text GitHub serves: the README must have
  a `Requirements` heading and must state the host range `package.json`
  declares. A repository whose checkout fails `readme` fails the remote check
  too, with the same sentence.
- File checks (does `exports["./client"]` point at a file that exists, does the
  root export `apply`) need the tree. npm runs `prepack` and `prepare` before
  `npm pack` creates the tarball, and `prepublishOnly` before `npm publish`
  does, so a package whose lifecycle hook builds those files publishes files it
  does not commit: those checks are **skipped with a note** instead of calling a
  working plugin broken. A plain `build` script is not a lifecycle hook and is
  not evidence by itself, because npm never runs it unless `prepack` or
  `prepare` calls it; put the build there if it produces shipped files.
- Public repositories work anonymously, but GitHub allows 60 requests an hour.
  Export `GH_TOKEN` (or `GITHUB_TOKEN`) to audit more than one or two.

To check a whole list in one pass, put one `owner/repo` per line in a file and
pass it with `--from` (`-` reads standard input):

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt
```

Repositories are read four at a time by default. `--jobs N` changes that width;
values above `8` are capped at `8`, and `--jobs 1` walks the list one repository
at a time, the timing the command had before batching. The output — and the
`--json` array — still follows the input list, and every verdict is the one the
sequential run produced, so a diff between two runs compares repositories rather
than scheduling.

When GitHub answers `403` or `429`, the shared quota is gone, so the batch stops
starting new repositories and marks every entry it could not read as
`rate-limited` instead of `clean` or `unreadable`. If the response carries
`x-ratelimit-reset` (or `retry-after`), the reset time is printed with the
verdict, and the remaining entries are reported without another request.

### Will this plugin install on my DSH?

The nineteen compatibility reports, from four repositories, all end with the same
question. Add `--host <version>` to a remote audit and it answers that question
for one repository. This is the output for `L3n3L/dsh-resume`, a real plugin
whose declared range stops before DSH 0.2.0, checked against the
`0.2.2-alpha.3` canary from the reports. The checked-in sample is a frozen 0.1.3
snapshot, so the line stays true as the upstream repository changes:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote L3n3L/dsh-resume --host 0.2.2-alpha.3
incompatible  L3n3L/dsh-resume  0.1.3 (host >=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0) [incompatible with dsh 0.2.2-alpha.3; declares ">=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0"]

summary: 1 repository — 0 clean, 1 failing (1 problem), 0 unreadable, 0 rate-limited
```

The sample defaults to that canary. Pass `--host` to ask the same frozen 0.1.3
manifest about the version you actually run; this is the same range against an
older stable host it accepts:

```sh
$ node scripts/compatibility-sample.mjs --host 0.1.5
clean         L3n3L/dsh-resume  0.1.3 (host >=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0) [compatible with dsh 0.1.5; declares ">=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0"]

summary: 1 repository — 1 clean, 0 failing (0 problems), 0 unreadable, 0 rate-limited
```

With an explicit `--host` the wrapper exits with the replayed command's status
(`0` for this compatible line, `1` for a version the range rejects), so it can
gate a CI step. The default form still exits `0` only after the documented
incompatible replay exited `1`. An invalid version such as `banana` reaches the
CLI's own `--host needs a complete DSH version` refusa

# Numes × DeepSeek Harness **Free models, smart retries, zero paid-fallback risk — as a local proxy in front of [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).** [![CI](https://github.com/wwewtech/numes-deepseek-harness/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wwewtech/numes-deepseek-harness/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE) [![No dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-none-6ead4a.svg)](tools/numes-free-failover.mjs) [![Node 18+](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-18%2B-339933.svg)](https://nodejs.org) [![Numes API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Numes-%240%20free%20route-8b5cf6.svg)](https://numes.ai/docs/models#free-models) [English](README.md) · **Русский** · **中文** · [Full setup (EN)](docs/SETUP.md) · [Full setup (RU)](docs/SETUP.ru.md) · [Full setup (中文)](docs/SETUP.zh.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) Listed in [vvlife/awesome-deepseek-harness-plugins](https://github.com/vvlife/awesome-deepseek-harness-plugins). Independent project — not affiliated with DeepSeek or Numes.
--- > ### What is this? > > [Numes](https://numes.ai) is an OpenAI-compatible model marketplace where some offers are **`$0`** — routed via `author/model:free`, they *cannot* fall back to a paid endpoint. > [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) is a plugin-based coding agent. > > This repo glues them together: **no DSH plugin needed**, one `Custom model API` form, one local proxy that never gives up and never spends a cent. --- ## ✨ What you get | Feature | Why it matters | |---|---| | 💸 **Hard `$0` route** | Every model id ends with `:free`, every request carries `provider.max_price {0,0}`, and Numes guarantees `:free` never falls back to paid. **Three guards, zero charge.** | | 🔁 **Never-give-up retries** | `503` on all free models? Wait `5s → 10s → 15s → 30s → 1m → 2m → 5m → 5m…` and walk the chain again. Exhausted free pools recover without you touching anything. | | 🤖 **Auto-discovery** | The free-model list refreshes from `GET /models` every 5 minutes. A removed offer drops out of routing; a newly-free model joins automatically. | | ⏱️ **`Retry-After` aware** | Numes says "wait 2s" on `429`/`503`? The proxy reads the hint and never waits *less* than the platform asked. | | 🚫 **Smart abort** | `401`/`402`/`403` (dead key, no funds) stop the rounds immediately — retrying a rejected key is pointless noise. | | 🔒 **Paid-model guard** | Send `moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro` (paid) instead of `...:free`? Instant `400` before any traffic leaves your machine. | | 📊 **`/status` dashboard** | One request shows the guard, the live chain, the retry state, and every counter. | | 🧩 **Zero dependencies** | One `.mjs` file, Node 18+, no `npm install`. The key is read from DSH's own credential store. | ## 🚀 Quick start (2 minutes) > Prefer installing as a DSH bundle? `dsh plugin --profile add github:wwewtech/numes-deepseek-harness` — the bundle merges `cordis.patch.yml` into the profile and registers the `numes-free` provider for you. You still need to run the proxy below. **Note**: the loader semantics replace the matched `llm-pi-ai` row's `config` wholesale — existing hand-edited providers on that row will be overwritten. Use `node tools/merge-providers.mjs --profile > numes-merge.yml` + `dsh --patch numes-merge.yml` to preserve them. Verify with `dsh --profile --dump-config | grep -A 4 "numes-free"`. Verify without manual edits: `dsh --profile --dump-config | grep -A 4 numes-free` — expected: the provider printed by the Loader. **1.** Create a Numes **inference key** at [numes.ai/dashboard/keys](https://numes.ai/dashboard/keys) (currency is permanent; free requests need a verified email). **2.** Run the proxy: ```bash node tools/numes-free-failover.mjs ``` ```text listening on http://127.0.0.1:8787 (chain of 9 free models) free guard: :free suffix + provider.max_price{0,0} on every request; paid routes impossible catalogue discovery: every 300s from GET /models ``` **3.** In DSH: **Settings → Models → Add model provider → Custom model API** | Field | Value | |---|---| | Provider ID | `numes-free` | | Base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1` | | Protocol | **OpenAI Chat Completions** | | API key | any placeholder (the real key stays in the proxy) | **4.** Pick `Numes free (auto-failover)` in the model picker. Done. > [!TIP] > No proxy wanted? Skip steps 2–3 and point DSH straight at `https://api.numes.ai/api/v1`, selecting the **`:free`** models yourself — see [docs/SETUP.ru.md](docs/SETUP.ru.md). The proxy only adds failover, retries, and discovery. ## 🏗️ How it works ``` DSH (agent, coding sessions) │ OpenAI Chat Completions ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────────┐ │ numes-free-failover 127.0.0.1:8787 │ │ │ guard: id ends with ":free"? │── no ──▶ 400 refused │ guard: max_price {0,0} always │ │ │ │ chain: 9 free models │ │ (auto-discovered, sticky) │ │ │ │ all failed? ─▶ wait ─▶ retry │ │ 5s→10s→15s→30s→1m→2m→5m→5m… │ │ (Retry-After honoured) │ │ │ │ 401/402/403? ──▶ stop now │ └─────────────────────────────────┘ │ Bearer key (never logged) ▼ Numes API ──▶ amazee.ai :free pool ──▶ $0 ``` ## 🎛️ Tuning | Variable | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `NUMES_PROXY_PORT` | `8787` | Listen port (`127.0.0.1` only) | | `NUMES_CHAIN` | *(auto)* | Pin your own free-model order | | `NUMES_PROXY_BACKOFF_MS` | `5000,…,300000` | Round delays; last repeats forever | | `NUMES_PROXY_MAX_ROUNDS` | `0` | Give up after N rounds (`0` = never) | | `NUMES_PROXY_DISCOVERY_MS` | `300000` | Catalogue refresh interval (`0` = off) | ## 🎯 Try it ```bash # what's the proxy up to? curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/status | jq .free,.retry # a real free request curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"auto","max_tokens":1500,"reasoning":{"effort":"none"}, "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say PONG"}]}' # → X-Numes-Free-Model: X-Numes-Free-Round: 1 # usage.cost: 0 ``` ## ⚠️ Honest limits - **`$0` ≠ unlimited.** Free offers appear and vanish with provider prices; auto-discovery keeps the list current but cannot conjure capacity. If every free offer is gone, rounds keep failing *honestly*. - **`$0` ≠ instant.** The free pool measured 50–85s to first token (short pings: ~3–8s). Set a generous `max_tokens` (1500+) — reasoning tokens eat the budget, and `max_tokens: 40` yields an empty answer with `finish_reason: "length"`. - **`$0` ≠ private.** Providers declare their own data policies; read them before sending secrets. The proxy itself never logs your key or prompts. - **Not a Numes or DeepSeek product.** Independent glue, verified on DSH Desktop 0.2.2-rc.3 with a USD key on 17 Nov 2026. DSH rc.4/rc.5 only change server-side search and bug fixes, not the provider setup this repo documents. ## 🖼️ Visual tour
Terminal DSH model picker (real screenshot) Retry flow
🛡️ `dsh-model-picker.png` and `dsh-model-list.png` are **real screenshots** from DSH Desktop 0.2.2-rc.3 showing the bundle-installed provider. `terminal.png` and `flow.png` are illustrative mockups. SVG originals in [`docs/assets/`](docs/assets/). --- ## 📚 Everything else | | | |---|---| | 🇷🇺 **Полный гайд (рекомендуется)** | [docs/SETUP.ru.md](docs/SETUP.ru.md) — от установки DSH до первого ответа, с разбором ошибок | | 🇬🇧 Full setup guide | [docs/SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md) — the same, in English | | 🇨🇳 **中文全指南** | [docs/SETUP.zh.md](docs/SETUP.zh.md) — 完整安装、排错与 API 用法 | | 🇨🇳 **中国人（README）** | [README.zh.md](README.zh.md) — 项目总览 | | 🔧 Proxy reference | [tools/README.md](tools/README.md) — every env var, header, and behaviour | | ⚙️ DSH config blocks | [configs/](configs/) — direct and proxy routes | | 📦 DSH bundle | [`.dsh-plugin/manifest.json`](.dsh-plugin/manifest.json) + root `package.json` — `dsh plugin add github:wwewtech/numes-deepseek-harness` | | 📋 Changelog | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) — what changed in each version | | 🛡️ Security & contributing | [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) · [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) | | 🧪 **Examples** | [`examples/`](examples/) — curl, Python, PowerShell, Node, tool-calls | | 📸 **Real screenshots** | [`dsh-model-picker.png`](docs/assets/dsh-model-picker.png) · [`dsh-model-list.png`](docs/assets/dsh-model-list.png) | ## ✅ What CI checks Every push runs [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml), which verifies the claims made above rather than trusting them: - the proxy parses, boots, and answers `/health` with a non-empty chain; - the **paid-model guard really returns `400`** for a non-free id, before any network I/O; - every relative Markdown link resolves; - no Numes key (or GitHub token) is committed; - each config lists only `:free` Numes ids; - the source still contains the guard, `max_price`, backoff, `Retry-After`, discovery, and fatal-abort code the README advertises; - the **root `package.json`** declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, `.dsh-plugin/manifest.json` references a real `cordis.patch.yml`, and the listed entry file exists; - **7 integration tests** (`tests/proxy.test.mjs`) covering the guard, `/health`, `/status`, `/v1/models`, chain override, unknown routes and bad JSON. Run the same checks locally: ```bash node tools/check-repo.mjs npm test ``` ## 📄 License [MIT](LICENSE). Not affiliated with DeepSeek or Numes. Applies Numes [ToS](https://numes.ai/legal/terms) and [AUP](https://numes.ai/legal/acceptable-use); no account automation, no quota evasion.

decision.reason: The same-commit patch only configures the official @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai provider. It requires a separately started tools/numes-free-failover.mjs proxy; it does not mount its own native Cordis plugin. A dsh.bundle.patch field alone does not make this provider configuration a native plugin.

# dsh-im-lark

把飞书 / Lark 机器人接到 DeepSeek Harness：在飞书里私聊机器人，等于在 Web 端对话。

两条互相独立的使用路径：

| 模式 | 开关 | 需要核心 | 行为 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **独立会话**（默认） | 接入飞书，关闭「接入我的超级助理」 | 否 | 插件自己建一个会话，直接在飞书里聊；文字命令、问题与审批提醒由插件处理 |
| **接入核心** | 接入飞书 + 接入我的超级助理 | 是 | 飞书当作 Web 端的一个入口：消息、命令、提醒整体交给核心 |

两种模式互斥：只有「接入我的超级助理」打开且核心服务在时才走核心，否则一律独立会话，
同一句话不会被两处处理。面板上的核心开关在没装核心时是禁用的。

## 能力

- **入站**：文本、富文本、图片、文件；语音/视频/表情包等给一句明确提示，不静默丢弃
- **出站**：Markdown 卡片、图片；长回答按字符与卡片体积双上限切段
- **引用回复**：回答引用触发它的那条消息，单聊与群里都成立
- **处理反馈**：收到消息先打 `Typing` 表情，处理完换成 `DONE`；失败只撤 `Typing`，不留「已完成」的假信号。飞书没有官方「正在输入」接口
- **卡片更新**：流式回答原地更新同一张卡片；超过平台限制（14 天、单卡 5 QPS）后改发新卡
- **交互卡片**：核心模式的**单问题**单选题与多选题在飞书里勾选后提交，结果交回核心；
  独立模式的单题提问同样发卡片（单选/多选都是勾选器，靠文案区分，必须点提交），其余仍走
  文字提醒。多问题与审批只发提示，请在 Web 端作答（核心要求一次提交全部问题，卡片回调
  做不到分题提交）；两者都支持「其他」输入
- **群聊**：只响应 @机器人 的消息（群聊权限只申请 @ 系列），不读全群
- **任务提醒**：独立模式下，回合跑得久（默认超过 30 分钟）会在结束时发一条带耗时与结论的提醒；回合失败或被外部中止时立刻提醒并带上原始错误。主人自己按的停止不算失败
- **面板**：Web 端插件页扫码一键创建应用，或手动填 App ID / App Secret；看连接状态、开关收发/核心接入、改消息行为；独立模式可调回合内插话、会话工作区、问题/审批提醒与长程任务提醒

> 提问卡片（勾选器 + 提交 + 「其他」输入）在独立模式与核心模式都已于真实飞书租户验收：
> 单选/多选靠卡片文案区分，提交后回传勾选项与「其他」输入。已知差异：独立模式勾了多项
> 会回一句提示并保留待答，核心模式的作答由核心校验，被拒时**没有可见反馈**（只有插件
> 调试日志）。`Typing` 表情与卡片排版随租户配置略有差异，以实际表现为准。

## 安装

正式版进 `latest`，预发布进频道标签（`stage` / `rc`），两者不会互相覆盖：

```bash
# 正式版
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-im-lark

# 预发布
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-im-lark@stage
```

从源码装（开发用）：

```bash
npm install
npm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add file:/绝对路径/dsh-im-lark
```

`file:` 依赖是**注入副本**，装进 profile 的 `node_modules` 后与仓库解耦：改了代码要
`npm run build`，再卸了重装才会同步到运行中的 Host。

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-im-lark
dsh plugin --profile web add file:/绝对路径/dsh-im-lark
```

重装后不用重启 `dsh web`：Host 半由热重载接管，浏览器刷新页面即可。打开
**设置 → 飞书机器人**（或 **插件 → dsh-im-lark**）填写凭据。

### 扫码创建应用

面板的「应用凭据」里点「扫码创建应用」，用飞书扫描二维码并在手机上确认。应用创建成功后凭据会自动保存并开始连接；二维码 1 小时内有效、仅限一位用户使用。

创建出来的应用仍要确认权限与事件订阅（见下一节）。如果长连接一直收不到消息，先检查「事件订阅」是否为**长连接**、是否订阅了 `im.message.receive_v1`。

## 飞书侧准备

1. 在[飞书开放平台](https://open.feishu.cn/app)创建**企业自建应用**，拿到 App ID 与 App Secret。
2. **添加应用能力 → 机器人**。
3. **权限管理**开通：
   - `im:message.p2p_msg:readonly`（接收单聊消息）
   - `im:message.group_at_msg:readonly`（接收群里 @机器人 的消息）
   - `im:message:send_as_bot`（以机器人身份发消息）
   - `im:resource`（上传/下载图片与文件）
   - 表情回应（可选）：控制台里与 reaction 相关的权限。没有也不影响主流程，
     「正在处理」提示会自动降级为不发
4. **事件与回调**：
   - 「事件订阅」选择**长连接**，订阅 `im.message.receive_v1`；
   - 「回调配置」添加 `card.action.trigger`（需要卡片交互时），同样走长连接
5. **发布版本**并等管理员审核通过；未发布前只有开发者自己能用。

> 长连接模式不需要公网地址、不需要配置请求网址。每个应用最多 50 条长连接，多实例部署时**只有一条**连接会收到事件，所以不要靠多开进程做水平扩展。

## 配置

静态配置写在 profile 的 patch 里，改完重启生效：

```yaml
- id: dsh-im-lark
  name: dsh-im-lark
  config:
    domain: feishu          # feishu（默认）或 lark（国际版）
    maxText: 2000           # 单条消息字符上限，超出自动切段
    typingIndicator: true   # 收到打 Typing，处理完换成 DONE
    replyStatus: false      # 回答末尾附加模型、耗时、token
    directBusyMode: steer   # 独立会话里回合进行中又来消息：steer 插话 / queue 排队（旧值 interrupt 会迁移成 steer）
    directWorkspaceId: ''   # 独立会话的工作区 id；留空用自动创建的默认工作区
    questionReminders: true # 独立模式下有问题/授权在等时发飞书提醒
    questionDelayMinutes: 5 # 提醒前等多久（0–120）：这段时间在 Web 端答完就不打扰
    longTaskReminders: true # 独立模式：回合耗时超过阈值时发完成提醒
    longTaskMinutes: 30     # 长任务阈值（1–1440 分钟）
    failureReminders: true  # 独立模式：回合失败或被外部中止时立刻提醒
```

面板能改的项会落到 `$DSH_HOME/.dsh-im-lark/config.json`，卸载重装后沿用。凭据单独存 `credentials.json`，目录 0700、文件 0600，日志与面板快照里只出现 App ID 尾号。

## 独立会话命令

| 命令 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `/help` | 命令列表 |
| `/new` | 开新会话 |
| `/sessions` | 列出最近会话，切到指定会话 |
| `/status` | 当前会话与运行状态 |
| `/stop` | 中止正在跑的回合 |
| `/trace` | 查看上一条回答的模型与耗时 |
| `/send <文本>` | 不经模型，直接发一段文本 |

## 命令行与斜杠命令

- **`/lark`**（Web 输入框）：`/lark <正文>` 把一段文字发到自己的飞书；`/lark status`
  看凭据与收件人是否就绪。不经模型。
- **`dsh-lark-send`**（终端 / 脚本）：`dsh-lark-send text <正文>`、`status`、`help`。
  收件人恒为主人，没有 `--to`；退出码 `0` 成功、`1` 发送失败、`2` 参数写错。

收件人恒为「主人」：独立模式是第一个在飞书里私聊机器人的人，核心模式是核心绑定的用户；还没有主人时会明确报错。

## 范围说明

- 独立模式：问题与工具授权在等主人时，插件发飞书提醒（延迟可调）：单题有选项的直接
  点卡片作答，多题/审批/自由输入仍用文字（回序号或选项文字）。长任务完成提醒仍由核心负责。
- 独立模式收到文件只给一句提示，不把文件内容送进会话；图片会作为输入附上。
- IM 卡片只承载单问题、有选项的交互；多问题/审批/自由输入交回 Web 端，避免出现
  「点了按钮但永远答不完」的卡。

## 限制（平台决定，不是实现取舍）

- 事件处理必须 **3 秒内** 返回，重活一律异步做
- 文本消息体 ≤ 150 KB，卡片 ≤ 30 KB，超了平台直接拒收
- 发消息 5 QPS（按用户 / 按群），插件内置限速与退避
- 同一张卡片可 PATCH 14 天、单卡 5 QPS；超时后改为新发消息
- 图片 ≤ 10 MB，文件 ≤ 30 MB，上传前本地先拦一道
- 编辑消息有次数上限，撤回窗口由管理员配置（常见 24 小时）
- 没有官方「正在输入」接口，只能用作表情作为弱提示

## 开发

```bash
npm run typecheck   # 类型检查（测试文件一起查）
npm test            # 单元测试
npm run build       # tsc 编译 host + esbuild 打 client 单文件
npm run verify      # 校验产物、依赖白名单、patch 只增不删
npm run check       # 上面四步全跑
```

目录：

```
index.ts             入口，转出 src/host/index.ts
src/host/            宿主侧：连接、入站、出站、卡片、桥接、独立会话、面板 RPC
src/client/          Web 面板（React，打成单文件 lib/client.js）
src/shared/          两侧共用的常量与版本
locale/              面板文案
docs/design/         方案设计
docs/protocol/       飞书开放平台事实（含来源链接）
docs/adr/            架构决策记录
```

改代码前读 `AGENTS.md`（文件规模、日志脱敏、不引新依赖等硬规则）。

### 门禁与发布

`npm run check` 是本地全量门禁，测试自包含：不依赖私有核心 `dsh-my-superagent`，
公开 CI 跑的就是同一套。

发布由 `.github/workflows/release.yml` 在 main 上完成（[ADR-0007](docs/adr/0007-发布流程与版本通道.md)）：
版本号三处同步（`package.json`、锁文件、`src/shared/version.ts`），正式版正文写
`docs/releases/v<版本>.md`；预发布不进 `docs/releases/`，Release 正文由 workflow 生成。
推 main 后自动打 tag、发 npm、建 Release：预发布只进 npm 的频道标签（`stage` / `rc`），
`latest` 只给正式版。

## 许可

MIT

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-mworks-ai

MWORKS AI for DeepSeek Harness — the same shape as the official **Syslab AI** and **Sysplorer AI** assistants: official MCP servers, official skills, and one place in the UI that reports what the agent can do.

## Install

Published on npm as [`dsh-mworks-ai`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-mworks-ai).

```bash
npm install --save-dev dsh-mworks-ai
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch` (`cordis.patch.yml`) and `dsh.client`, so a harness that loads it as a bundle picks up both the MCP rows and the UI section with no extra wiring.

## What it adds

| Surface | What you get |
|---|---|
| Tools | `mcp__mworks_syslab__*` (8 tools: Julia execution, environment detection, help search, MATLAB→Julia mapping) and `mcp__mworks_sysplorer__*` (15 tools: session, library, model, check, translate, simulate, layout, results, plotting, API/model docs, resources). Plus `mworks_environment` (installation + live MCP state), `mworks_mcp_status`, and `mworks_mcp_restart`. |
| Instructions | The official MWORKS working rules: Syslab needs `read_syslab_skill` → `detect_syslab_toolboxes` before any code execution; prefer `Ty*` packages; confirm APIs from local help; call `session_manager` before other Sysplorer tools; keep outputs out of the installation directories. Plus the recovery rule: a MWORKS call that stops answering is not fixed by retrying — read `mworks_mcp_status` and rebuild the server instead. |
| UI | A **Runtime environment** section on this bundle's own page under **Plugins**, below the configuration the Plugin Manager draws. It lists the detected Syslab and Sysplorer installations and versions, the Julia runtime, both MCP servers with their live connection state, and the MWORKS skills this session can call, with **Re-detect** and, for a server that is not connected, **Reconnect**. The section renders nothing on any other plugin's page. Nothing is added to the conversation. |

## Why the MCP servers are owned by the MCP manager

`cordis.patch.yml` contains only this plugin's own row: the two servers are contributed at runtime through `ctx.mcpManager.register()`, not as bare `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` rows. That buys two things a bare row cannot:

- **Observable state.** A server reports `connecting` / `connected` / `reconnecting` / `failed` with its registered tool count and last error, in the section and in `mworks_mcp_status`.
- **In-place recovery.** `mcpManager.restart(name)` remounts just that MCP child.

Both matter because of a failure mode that otherwise stays invisible: when Sysplorer is restarted underneath a running session, the MCP child keeps running but stays attached to the old engine port. It emits no close and no error, so the client bridge has nothing to reconnect on, and every subsequent call blocks until `toolCallTimeoutMs` (five minutes) expires. Killing/remounting the child is what re-runs engine discovery and re-attaches to the live port — verified by killing a wedged child and watching a fresh one attach to the new port.

## Skills

The MWORKS skills are **registered by this plugin from the copies inside the MWORKS installation** (`<Sysplorer>/Tools/sysplorer_mcp/resources/modeling_skills` and `<Syslab>/Tools/syslab-skills`), the same way a skill bundle registers its own `skills/` directory. That matters because the MWORKS installers also copy those bundles into an AI client's folder (`%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\skills` for OpenCode), and no DeepSeek Harness provider scans that path on its own — without an explicit contribution, the skills reach the catalog only when some other plugin happens to read that directory.

- **No dependency on OpenCode.** OpenCode need not be installed and its folder need not exist; the plugin reads the installation instead.
- **No interference.** The plugin writes nothing into any client's skill folder, and it fills a gap only: when the registry already resolves any MWORKS skill, it registers nothing, so it never duplicates or overrides another provider's decisions (including a per-skill disable list).
- **Only MWORKS skills are taken from shared folders.** Every bundle counts inside the installation directories; from a shared client directory such as OpenCode's, only names MWORKS owns (`ty-`, `syslab-`, `ta-`, `modelica-library-workflow`, `sysplorer-mds-docs`) are claimed.
- **Gap fill by name.** A skill the registry already resolves is left to whichever provider supplies it; only missing names are registered from the installation.
- **Opt out.** Set `registerSkills: false` on this plugin's row to stop the contribution entirely, for example when another provider manages the MWORKS skills and you want its per-skill filtering to win.
- **Names come from frontmatter.** Folded (`>-`) and literal (`|`) descriptions are parsed, and each registration carries a directory `resourceBase`, so a skill's `references/`, `templates/` and `tests/` resolve against the installed bundle.

The Runtime environment section and `mworks_environment` report what the registry actually resolves and say whether that answer came from the registry or from the on-disk scan.

## Configuration

Server definitions (command, args, env, cwd, timeouts, reconnect policy) live in the `SERVERS` table of `lib/index.js`. Defaults:

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `toolCallTimeoutMs` | 300000 | A model check, translation or simulation can legitimately take minutes. This is also the worst-case cost of a wedged call, so lower it if your simulations are short. |
| `startupTimeoutMs` | 60000 | Sysplorer's first attach can take a while. |
| `reconnect` | enabled, 500 ms → 5 s backoff, 10 attempts | Recovers a child that actually exits. It cannot see a *wedged* child, which is what `mworks_mcp_restart` is for. |

A profile must mount `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-manager` (the Web and Desktop profiles do). Without it the plugin still loads, but contributes no MCP servers, and `mworks_environment` says the state cannot be reported or repaired.

## Requirements

- A local MWORKS installation. Paths are listed in the `SERVERS` table of `lib/index.js`; the Runtime environment section and `mworks_environment` report what is actually found.
- The profile must mount `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill` (every standard profile does) for the skills to reach the agent, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-manager` for the MCP servers. Both are part of the Web and Desktop profiles.

## Startup parameters that matter

`cordis.patch.yml` inserts one row, this plugin's own; the two MCP servers are contributed at runtime (see above). Two flags cost a debugging session each:

| Where | Detail |
|---|---|
| Syslab args | `--syslab-display-mode=nodesktop` keeps Julia calls off an open Syslab desktop; `--syslab-root` is mandatory or the server panics. |
| Sysplorer entry | Start through `Tools/sysplorer_mcp/main.py`, the launcher that exports `MCP_DEPLOY_ROOT`. Starting the inner `main.py` breaks `resources_retrieval` while `tools/list` still looks healthy. |

## Checks

`test/` holds four checks that run without the app:

```bash
node test/host-check.mjs       # MCP registration, tools, routes, status mapping
node test/render-check.mjs     # renders the detail-page section
node test/class-check.mjs      # every class used is defined, every rule is used
node test/metadata-check.mjs   # display metadata and artwork limits
```

`host-check.mjs` pins the MCP-manager contract (including that Sysplorer starts through the launcher and Syslab runs `nodesktop`), and `render-check.mjs` is the one that matters for UI changes: it walks the real element tree and asserts the contract (only `plugins.detail.section`, null on foreign pages, no fetch before the page opens), so a component that throws — which makes the host blank the section — fails the check instead of shipping.

## Limits

- All MWORKS capability comes from the installed products. Without Syslab the Julia tools fail; without Sysplorer the Modelica tools fail. The section says which paths are missing instead of guessing.
- The plugin only reads paths and version files. It writes nothing into the MWORKS directories, and it never starts a GUI.
- The section reports installation state, not connection health: the tool counts are what the official servers declare (8 and 15), and calling a tool is the only proof that one answered. Run `mworks_environment`, or open this bundle's page under Plugins, to see what was detected.
- Turning the bundle off removes both MCP connections, the tool, the instructions and the button.

## Releasing

`package.json` holds the version; the git tag and the GitHub Release must match it (`v` prefix is stripped before comparing).

1. Bump `version` in `package.json` and `npm test`.
2. Commit, then tag and push:

   ```bash
   git tag -a v1.0.1 -m "dsh-mworks-ai 1.0.1"
   git push origin main --tags
   ```

3. Publish a GitHub Release for that tag. `.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml` runs on `release: published`: it verifies the tag against `package.json`, runs the checks, and publishes to npm (skipping versions that already exist).

Authentication prefers npm **Trusted Publishing** (OIDC, no secret) and falls back to the `NPM_TOKEN` repository secret, so a granular token works until the trusted publisher is configured.

# dsh-quiz-tutorial · 刷题场 [English](README.en.md) · 中文 [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-dsh--plugin-6f42c1)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) 一个 DeepSeek Harness（dsh）插件：把任意复习内容变成**题集**，在 Web UI 里逐题练习—— 题目在左，**逐步手算解析**在右，答错的题自动进**错题本**，并支持用 `/skill dsh-quiz` 直接让 Agent 出题。

用 /skill dsh-quiz 生成的「K-means 与 GMM 专项」题集；右侧是逐题手算解析。

## 功能 - **题集**：左侧列表切换；内置 CNN / 机器学习概念题，也可以按任意学科生成新题集。 - **题目 + 解析**：矩阵输入、2–6 个选项；作答后右侧展开正确答案、用到的公式、 **带中间矩阵的逐步手算**、易错点、每个错误选项的诊断。 - **公式渲染**：题面/解析/速查卡里的 `$...$`、`_{...}`/`^{...}`、`\frac`、`\sum`、希腊字母 等会渲染成上下标与 Unicode 符号（轻量渲染器，不执行 HTML、不加载外部资源）。 - **错题本**：答错自动收录（跨题集），支持筛选、看解析、重做、标记已订正、 「重练全部未订正」队列；答对自动订正。 - **`/skill dsh-quiz` 出题**：在输入框输入 `/skill dsh-quiz 主题`，Agent 会查重、 自己把答案和中间量算对，再保存成题集。 - **删除 / 隐藏题集**：自建题集卡片右上角 × 真正删除（同时清掉该题集在本地的作答与错题 记录）；内置题集 × 隐藏，列表底部可恢复。 - **本地优先**：题集与作答/错题记录都在本机（题集在 `~/.dsh/dsh-quiz/decks/`，进度在 localStorage），没有账号、没有遥测。 - 键盘 `A–F` / `1–6` 选答案，`←` / `→` 切题；深/浅色主题跟随宿主 token。 ## 安装 需要 dsh web（0.2.0-rc.2 或更新；1.0.1 起两条 Web 路由复用 dsh 的 `connection` 信任栅栏，因此要求 Host 提供该服务）。包已发布到 npm： ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-quiz-tutorial ``` 备选安装方式（npm 不可用时从 GitHub 装同一个包）： ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add github:xiaobin118/dsh-quiz-tutorial ``` > 如果装过早期的开发 bundle `dsh-quiz`，先移除它（`dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-quiz`）， > 避免两个 bundle 注册同一个 `quiz` 面板。 装好后重启一次 `dsh web`（Host 侧的路由与技能不会热加载），刷新浏览器页面。 打开左侧栏的 **刷题场**。 > 如果是从仓库本地开发安装（`plugin_manager install_bundle` / 旧 `dsh-quiz` 包）， > 先移除旧 bundle 再装这个包，避免两个 bundle 注册同一个 `quiz` 面板。 ## 用 /skill 出题 在对话输入框里： ```text /skill dsh-quiz 自编码器与 VAE ``` 技能会要求 Agent： 1. 先 `quiz_list_decks` 查重； 2. 设计 5–10 题，**自己算对**每道题的答案和全部中间量； 3. 用 `quiz_save_deck` 保存完整题集 JSON； 4. 提示你打开刷题场、点「刷新题集」。

/skill dsh-quiz 生成题集后，Agent 回报题表；打开刷题场刷新即可练习。

也可以直接对 Agent 说「用 quiz_save_deck 按刚才复习的内容出一套题」。 ## 错题本 - 答错的题自动收录，记录错误次数、最近出错时间、上次错选项； - 筛选「未订正 / 已订正 / 全部」；每题可 **看解析 / 重做 / 标记已掌握 / 移出**； - **重练全部未订正**按最近出错顺序生成队列，答对自动标已订正，答错留在错题本； - 「清空已订正」二次确认。 ## 删除 / 隐藏题集 鼠标移到左侧题集卡片上，右上角出现 **×**： - **自建题集**：真正删除 `~/.dsh/dsh-quiz/decks/.json`，不可恢复；删除成功后该题集的 作答、错题记录和隐藏标记会一起清掉，不会污染之后同 id 的题集（包括恢复出来的内置版本）； - **内置题集**：从列表隐藏，安装包里的文件不动；列表底部「恢复隐藏的题集（N）」恢复； - 所有题集都隐藏时，主区域会显示恢复按钮； - 隐藏只作用于内置题集；从错题本点「看解析 / 重做」会自动把对应的隐藏题集恢复显示， 保证打开的是这道题所属的题集。 ## 题集格式 题集是纯 JSON：`id / title / subject / description / notes / questions`，每道题包含 `prompt / inputs / options / answer / formula / steps / pitfall`。 - 文件名必须是 `.json`；与内置题集同 id 表示「用户覆盖版本」； - 单套题集序列化后 ≤ 512 KiB，保存前按字节检查，超限直接报错、不写文件； - 字段超长会报错而不是静默截断；题目 id 重复会报错而不是改名； - 公式用 Unicode 或 `$...$` + `_{...}`/`^{...}` 写，支持常见 LaTeX 命令，但不是完整 LaTeX。 完整字段、约束、校验规则与公式写法见 [docs/deck-format.md](docs/deck-format.md)； 给 Agent 的出题规范见 [skill.md](skill.md)。 内置题集的数字（**包括干扰项**）由 [tools/gen_decks.py](tools/gen_decks.py) 计算并断言选项 唯一，不是手抄的： ```sh python3 tools/gen_decks.py # 重新生成 decks/*.json 并打印每道题的答案 python3 tools/gen_decks.py --check # 只校验仓库里的题集与脚本输出一致 ``` ## 安全与隐私 - 两条 Web 路由（`GET /dsh-quiz/decks`、`POST /dsh-quiz/decks/delete`）在**任何**处理之前 调用 dsh 的 `connection.requestRejection(req)`：Host/Origin 栅栏 + 浏览器会话校验； 缺失/空 `Host` 直接拒绝，`POST` 必须是 `application/json`； - 没有 `connection` 服务时路由 fail-closed（503），不会退化成匿名可读/可删； - 题集内容只作为 React 文本渲染（公式渲染器同样不注入 HTML），插件不发外部请求、不读凭据、 不做遥测。 ## 内置题集 - `ml-cnn`：CNN 卷积 / 池化计算专项（10 题，含单通道卷积、零填充、步长、多通道、 ReLU、最大/平均/重叠/全局池化） - `ml-core`：机器学习核心概念（5 题，过拟合、正则化、偏差-方差、precision/recall、数据泄漏） ## 开发 不需要构建，纯 ESM JavaScript： ``` index.js Host：/dsh-quiz/decks 路由、三个 quiz_* 工具、dsh-quiz 技能注册 client.js Web UI 的构建产物（DSH 只加载这一个文件，勿手改） client/src/ Web UI 源码，按职责拆分： base·locale·styles·text·math·state（宿主无关） components·notebook·page·panel（React 组件与插件注册） decks/*.json 内置题集 skill.md /skill 出题规范 tools/gen_decks.py 内置题集的生成与验算脚本 tools/build_client.mjs 把 client/src/*.js 拼成受版本控制的 client.js（无第三方依赖） test/*.test.js node:test 回归测试（题集、校验上限、存储契约、路由栅栏、客户端） docs/ 截图与题集格式文档 ``` DSH 的客户端模块系统只服务每个包的一个 bundle（`exports["./client"]`），并且只把 `require` 解析到平台模块表，无法 import 包内相对模块，所以客户端源码在 `client/src/`、 运行产物仍是单个 `client.js`： ```sh npm run build:client # 改完 client/src/*.js 后重新生成 client.js npm run check # 语法检查 + 确认 client.js 与源码同步 npm test # node --test（无依赖、无网络） python3 tools/gen_decks.py --check # 内置题集与生成脚本一致 ``` 本地测试建议用单独的 dsh profile / DSH_HOME，避免影响日常会话。Host 代码更新后需要 重启 `dsh web`；只改 `client.js` 时刷新页面即可。 ## 更新日志 ### 1.0.1 安全与数据完整性修复（针对 1.0.0 的独立审计）： - 两条 Web 路由接入 dsh 的 `connection` 信任栅栏（Host/Origin + 浏览器会话），空 `Host` 拒绝， `POST` 要求 `application/json`；没有 `connection` 时 fail-closed； - 题集大小改为统一的字节契约：保存前超过 512 KiB 直接报错、不落盘，读取同样按字节判断； - 文本字段超长改为**报错**而不是静默截断；题目 id 重复改为报错而不是静默改名； - 文件名与 `` 不一致的手写题集会被跳过并写进 `errors`，删除/列表/保存使用同一地址； - 删除题集时清理它的作答、错题记录与隐藏标记；从错题本打开隐藏题集会先恢复显示； - 题面/解析/速查卡的公式改为轻量渲染（`$...$`、`_{...}`/`^{...}`、`\frac`、希腊字母等）， 不再直接显示 `_{...}` 原文；`skill.md`、`docs/deck-format.md` 统一了写法约定； - 修正 `skill.md` / `docs/deck-format.md` 的示例（2×2 输入却写 4×4 输出 + 池化的矛盾）， 示例改为完整可算的 1×1 结果；内置题集 `ml-cnn` 的干扰项改为脚本计算； - 新增 `node:test` 回归测试与 CI（`npm run check`、`npm test`、生成脚本 `--check`）。 ## 贡献 欢迎任何形式的贡献：新学科题集、UI/交互、zh/en 翻译、Host 代码、文档、bug 报告。 - 提交前读 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)；题集贡献请遵守 [docs/deck-format.md](docs/deck-format.md) 与 [skill.md](skill.md) 的「答案必须自己算对」规则； - 新功能先开 issue 或 discussion 说明场景，避免大改方向不一致； - 市场条目/新题集/截图都欢迎 PR。 ## License [MIT](LICENSE)
