fullManifest.name: bothouse-pet
fullManifest.description: bothouse 自带的桌宠：fork 自 dsh-pet（MIT，PC2005-cloud），右键菜单接 bothouse 的角色、用量和任务板。吃白饭的蓝色大肥鱼，赖在 DeepSeek Harness 里不走了。平时爱玩魔方、爱吃各种零食、偶尔打个盹，闲不住就在桌面上溜达两圈，被你拖来甩去也照旧赖着；你忙起来它跟着忙前忙后，也会帮你打理余额钱包，闲下来爱碎碎念，还乐意陪你唠两句。
_comment: bothouse fork：上游 PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet c25386848f70f6e40902e4376f6e7b1e196bc326，改动与同步方法见 BOTHOUSE.md；peerDependencies 全标可选（独立模式用 shims 替身，bothouse 不装 DSH）；assets/webm 出包时由 scripts/bothouse-fetch-assets.mjs 下载
main: lib/index.js —— 宿主半侧入口（Cordis 插件：name/inject/apply）
icon —— 插件图标（DSH 插件管理页显示）：相对 package.json 的图片路径，只认 svg/png/jpg/jpeg/webp，≤256 KiB，realpath 后必须留在包目录内；读取方是 dsh-app-boot 的 iconOf，会内联成 base64 data URL 塞进 meta.icon
exports['./client'] —— 浏览器半侧入口，DSH 模块系统按它提供 /plugins/dsh-pet/client.js
dsh.bundle.patch —— 声明本包是 bundle，patch 文件是 cordis.patch.yml（安装后自动进层栈）
dsh.client —— 声明浏览器半侧的注入依赖和平台（web）

dsh.compatibility.dshReleases —— 对官方 DSH 完整版本逐项声明 compatible/incompatible/unknown；只写宽泛范围不算证据，商城最新三版至少需要一个 compatible。列表只保最新三版，新增一版就删最旧一版：DSH 自己只按 engines.dsh 与 peerDependencies 判定能不能装，这份列表不进安装闸门，无限叠加只会变成维护负担
files —— npm publish 只发这些目录/文件（assets/webm 播放资源（VP9-alpha，浏览器 Chrome/Edge/Firefox 与桌面模式共用）；Safari/HEVC 兼容由仓库流水线支持、fork 定制，不随包发布；assets/preview 的 GIF 仅 README 展示、不入包）
scripts.encode:webm —— 转码管线（step03 母版 → assets/webm 640×360 VP9-alpha）
scripts.build —— 构建完整产物 + files 收敛（node scripts/prepare.js）。克隆后手动跑一次；npm publish / npm pack 由 prepack 自动调用

scripts.prepack —— 发布前链：build（构建）→ typecheck/lint/format → prepack-check（素材健康检查）→ check:openapi。构建只挂这里：npm 11 会把 prepare 判为未批准的安装脚本，而 scripts/prepare.js 不随包发布（files 白名单只留 ensure-electron.mjs），用户一旦按提示批准就必然 ENOENT 失败
bin.dsh-pet-standalone —— 独立模式 CLI（构建产物 lib/standalone.js）：不打开 DSH 直接跑桌宠，把插件的宿主半边跑在伪 ctx 上；tsdown 的第二个入口负责构建，源码见 src/standalone/
peerDependencies —— 运行时由宿主（DSH）提供的模块，本包不打包它们
engines —— Node.js 兼容下限（由运行依赖 @electron/get@5.1.0 的 engines 决定）

scripts.prepack: npm run build && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run check:cycles && npm run check:runtime && npm run format:check && node scripts/prepack-check.js && npm run check:openapi
scripts.bothouse:pack: node scripts/bothouse-fetch-assets.mjs && tsdown && node scripts/build-desktop-core.mjs && npm pack --ignore-scripts

# dsh-pet 🐾 一只住在 DeepSeek Harness 里的桌面宠物，一百余个透明动画，可多开、能上桌面。 安装与完整文档：**** 许可：代码 MIT；素材禁止商用；二创在公开渠道须署名（同上链接）。
# bothouse **English** ｜ [中文](README.zh-CN.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/zuiho-kai/bothouse?style=flat-square&color=e8833a&label=release)](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-4a7c59?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS%20%C2%B7%20Windows%20%C2%B7%20Linux-555?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/releases) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/zuiho-kai/bothouse?style=flat-square&color=f2b33d)](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/stargazers) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join-5865F2?style=flat-square&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/aJmcnrt5ZB) **Put someone else's agent to work for you: a friend's Claude Code or Codex joins your group chat, and one @mention gets it started.** Bring your own AIs too: a team-lead AI splits the work and hands it out; they all share one memory. [Video](#video) · [Why](#why) · [Where to start](#usage) · [Install](#install) · [How it works](#how) · [Features](#features) · [Memory](#memory) · [Platforms](#platforms) · [Compare](#compare) · [Roadmap](#roadmap) · [Community](#community) · [Docs](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) · [Discord task forum](bridge/docs/task-forum.md)

**Watch it in 3 minutes** — one message goes in; the crew splits the work, does it and hands it back. Click the cover to play.

```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/main/install.sh | sh ``` ## Why I had Claude Code, Codex and DeepSeek open at once across two screens, and getting them to work together was a pain. So I put them all in one Discord group, let one of them hand out the work, and gave them a shared memory. No extra account, no extra subscription — you direct them from your computer, phone or browser. **The most common way people use it now: borrowing someone else's agents.** zzzx0757 in our group works this way every day with the author's (zuiho-kai) agents: he @mentions the lead AI in Discord, and the work goes out — the Codex role writes the code, the DeepSeek role polishes the copy — and the results come back to him. Your friend's Claude and Codex become staff on loan: no extra subscription just to generate images, no six people sharing one login. One computer stays on, and the whole group can hand out work. This repo is built the same way: I hand out work in the group, the agents each take a piece, one that wasn't involved reviews it, and then it gets merged. ## Where to start | What you have | Where to start | | --- | --- | | **A friend's agents** | Have a friend who runs bothouse invite you to their group, or bring their roles into yours. @mention one and it starts; nothing to install on your side. | | **Several AI command-line tools** | The setup wizard (see [Install](#install)): each role gets one of your signed-in AI command-line tools ("CLIs" below). | | **One model, one account** | Create several members on the same model, each with its own job. See [A team from one CLI](docs/single-cli-team.en.md). | | **DSH** (DeepSeek Harness, DeepSeek's own AI assistant app) | Say "install bothouse-dsh for me" in DSH, or run `bothouse module add dsh`. See [bothouse in DSH](docs/platforms/dsh.en.md). | ## Install Install with one command, then run `bothouse` to open the setup wizard in your browser: pick a platform, connect your bots, choose a local CLI for each role, and you are ready. ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/main/install.sh | sh ``` The Windows command, package downloads and the background service are in [Getting started](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md). On macOS, daemon install and restart allow a 30-second window for launchd to remove and reload the old job. If loading still fails, follow the error's recovery command; `bothouse daemon start` loads the saved service definition. **Let an AI agent install it for you:** give Claude Code, Codex or any agent CLI this repo link and say "install bothouse and connect it to Discord". The agent-side steps are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#用户说配-discord--飞书把这个配好接上-discord). ## How it works Only three ideas to learn: - **The team-lead AI** ("the lead" in the docs) — the AI you talk to in each chat channel. It splits real work and hands it out by skill and quota, so five AIs in one group still don't talk over each other. The others reply when you mention or name them. - **Workspaces** — big jobs (more than about ten minutes, or code changes and tests) go to a separate job channel with a handoff that carries your original words, the scope and what "done" looks like. Chat never stalls; one workspace, one job. The lead keeps a task board, and the bridge looks at every job every ten minutes. Results come back with proof, and only decisions that need you come back to chat. This is what we call **team mode**. - **Shared memory** — every role reads and writes the same Markdown notes, so whoever picks up a job already knows the background. See [Memory](#memory). Jobs can return results in batches: accepting a batch keeps the job and workspace open, while accepting the final report closes the job. Workspace agents use `ws-up --report --batch` for intermediate results and `--final` (the default) for the final handback; see the [workspace playbook](bridge/contrib/lead/PLAYBOOK.zh-CN.md). More detail — who replies when nobody is named, the nightly review, guardrails, switching the lead by hand — is in [How the team works](docs/readme-details.en.md#how-the-team-works). ## Features | You want | How bothouse helps | | --- | --- | | **Someone else's agent working for you** | A friend adds their Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and others to your group; you @mention one to hand it a job and the result comes back to you. As long as their computer is on, you can do it from your phone. | | **An AI team of your own** | Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, DSH, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Grok and more; each role has its own name, persona and session. | | **A team from one account** | Several members on one model, each with its own job; they hand work to each other by mention. | | **The chat apps you use** | Discord, Feishu, QQ or DSH; Discord and Feishu have phone apps, so you can hand out work from bed. | | **Long jobs stay on track** | Handoffs carry your original words; a second AI with a clean context checks the result; "fixed" needs evidence. | | **A nightly review** | Fixes and dedupes what was noted during the day; your repeated corrections become draft rules that apply only after you approve. | | **Manage it from your phone** | A web dashboard: who is busy, quota used, edit personas, add a note to running work. | Also: [team desk](docs/readme-details.en.md#team-desk) — a pixel office that shows the team at work; [remote pairing](docs/readme-details.en.md#remote-pairing) — run your team from another computer or your phone with a six-digit code; [per-channel model and reasoning](docs/model-and-reasoning.md); [role packs and avatars](docs/readme-details.en.md#roles-and-avatars); [optional image generation](docs/readme-details.en.md#image-generation).

Task board: what each workspace is doing and what landed today, at a glance.
Team desk: who is working on what, live; every light is a real event.

Roles: which CLI each role runs, what it is busy with, which model — pause or restart in one click.
Library: personas and avatars come in packs; pick one and it is ready to work.
_Top left: real channel footage. The rest: the author's own team desk and dashboard._ ### Characters (optional) Each role can also wear a persona and an avatar — handy if you want your team to have faces and personalities. The author's own team looks like this; pick from [role packs and avatars](docs/readme-details.en.md#roles-and-avatars), or skip it and keep the plain tools.

## Memory you can see The team's memory is a plain folder of Markdown files. Each incoming message first looks up the relevant pages; a nightly review fixes what was written down wrong. You can read and edit it directly; Git records every change and pushes it to your own private GitHub repo, so the memory follows you to another computer. - **Only the titles go in:** each turn picks the related memories by keyword and injects their titles and line numbers; a role opens the full text when it needs it. It costs very little and cuts rework — fewer "I already told you that". The idea came from vLLM. - **Light on cost:** no knowledge-graph CRUD and no always-on vector store, so cost and memory use stay small. - **Memory forum:** the panel's "Memory forum" page scores each memory as a reply — upvotes, downvotes, how often it was pushed and quoted — so a wrong memory falls down instead of being repeated. See [dispatcher and team memory](docs/ccm-and-wiki.md) (Chinese) and the [Wiki galaxy](docs/readme-details.en.md#wiki-galaxy). ## Platforms | Platform | Status | Capabilities | | --- | --- | --- | | Discord | Full support | Multiple roles, mentions, task handoffs, teammate status and log channels; slash commands in servers and DMs | | Feishu (Lark) | Single role | Conversation with one connected role | | QQ official bot | Manual setup | Group/private chat, group @user and @everyone; see [QQ Bot setup](bridge/docs/qqbot.md) | | DSH desktop app / web | Experimental | A Channels page inside the DeepSeek Harness desktop app (default) or DSH web; see [DSH](docs/platforms/dsh.en.md) | QQ via OneBot/NapCat, remote access from your phone with Tailscale, and hardware bodies for roles are in [Platform details](docs/readme-details.en.md#platform-details). ## bothouse and other projects **Most of them are one agent with a crew of sub-agents. bothouse puts the several AIs you already use into one group chat, splits the work between them, and gives them one shared memory.** **Which to pick**: for a personal assistant you can reach anywhere and that learns you, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent are mature; to watch several coding agents race side by side, pick Orca; if you only use DSH and want a few bots, there are Tobs and DS Bot. If you already have several AI CLIs and want them to split the work in one group and share one memory — say it before bed, collect results in the morning — pick bothouse. Many of these can be used together.
Side-by-side tables People often ask: DeepSeek now ships its own agent, and there are Tobs, DS Bot, OpenClaw and more — how is bothouse different? - **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** is DeepSeek's official open-source agent framework, still a developer preview: agent teams are experimental, and there's no built-in long-term memory unless you plug one in. bothouse's assignment, task board and shared memory are in daily use already — and DSH itself can join as one of the teammates. - **Tobs and DS Bot** are community bot projects built on DSH; every bot in the team runs on DSH. bothouse isn't tied to one agent: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and DSH each take their own jobs in the same group. | | What it is | Which AIs | How several AIs work together | Memory | Where you chat | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **bothouse** | **A coordination layer on your own computer + web panel** | **Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, DSH; Grok and more; OpenAI-compatible APIs** | **The lead role hands work to separate workspaces; task board; one thread per job** | **One shared Markdown wiki, reviewed nightly** | Discord, self-hosted web, Feishu, QQ, DSH web (experimental) | | [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) | DeepSeek's official agent framework (developer preview) | DeepSeek by default; other providers can be added | Subagents; agent teams are experimental | No built-in long-term memory; memory plugins can be added | Its own desktop app and web UI | | [Tobs](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot) | Bot plugin built on DSH | Models configured in DSH | @ whoever you need; assignments | One Git repo per bot | Feishu, Slack, Discord, QQ, WeChat | | [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot) | Desktop app / plugin / Docker built on DSH | Models configured in DSH | A chief bot runs the team; group admins coordinate | Memory per bot and per group | In the app | Mature personal assistants and coding tools get compared too: | | What it is | How several AIs work together | Memory | How bothouse differs | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) | Personal AI assistant with pluggable harnesses (Claude, Codex and more), 20+ chat apps | Team preset: a coordinator delegates to researcher, writer and reviewer | Sessions split per agent; Memory Wiki shared by default, can be split per agent | One assistant with swappable engines vs several signed-in CLIs working side by side in one group | | [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) | Self-improving personal assistant, any model | Isolated subagents in parallel | Manages its own memory, writes its own skills | It learns one person; bothouse gives a team one shared memory | | [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) | Multi-agent coding IDE using your own CLIs | Several agents race on one task; merge the best | Left to each CLI | It has you watch the race; bothouse lets you hand it off and walk away | | [LobeHub](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub) | Open-source agent workspace (web, desktop, mobile; cloud or self-hosted), 40+ model providers, can bring in Claude Code and Codex | Agent Team: sequential, parallel, iterative or debate; delegated tasks | Structured memories you can review and edit | A full workspace you move into vs a small program that drives your signed-in CLIs in the group you already use, with one Git-tracked Markdown memory | Others people ask about: | | What it's good at | What bothouse adds | | --- | --- | --- | | [Raft](https://www.testingcatalog.com/raft-1-0-puts-ai-agents-in-team-mode/) | People and agents in one new Slack-like workspace | No new app: plugs into the Discord, Feishu or web you already use; open source and self-hostable | | [Cindy](https://github.com/makecindy/cindy) | One client for Claude Code and Codex; switch models without losing context | The lead role splits the work and hands it out, so you don't have to | | [Tencent Mavis](https://technode.com/2026/05/21/tencent-unveils-mavis-ai-assistant-that-turns-pcs-into-conversational-interfaces/) | System-level assistant: files, PC and phone apps | Several AIs split project work: code, research, review | | [magpie](https://github.com/yetone/magpie) / [cc-switch](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch) | One place to manage model providers | Different layer: they decide which model, bothouse decides who takes which job and what the team remembers — use them together | | [llm-wiki](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/llm-wiki) | Turns sessions into a layered wiki memory | bothouse's memory builds on it and shares it across roles |
## Roadmap - **Share across people:** bring every teammate's Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and DeepSeek into one group, so one person tunes the AI and the whole team uses it — shared lessons from the nightly review, and each person's own standards and habits remembered separately. (Splitting work inside one group already works — see [How it works](#how).) - **Claim before starting:** lock assignments so two members never start the same task. - **Specialists on demand:** "publish to the App Store" spins up a specialist that reads prior decisions, does the job and exits. - **Role packs and a plugin marketplace:** personas, memory templates and tools in one-step bundles; browse community roles. - **Portable memory and semantic search:** carry the Wiki between computers and models, with semantic retrieval beside keyword search. - **Automatic workspace cleanup:** clear context after the last assignment so the next task starts fresh. - **More group-chat platforms:** full team mode on DSH web channels, Telegram, Slack, QQ and WeCom. - **Team-wide rules and skills:** push the team's rules, skills and tool settings to every member's computer in one step. - **Deep support for popular DSH plugins:** reuse the DSH plugin ecosystem, with deep support for the popular plugins. - **Hardware:** give a role a small ESP32 round-screen body with [bothouse-iot](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse-iot) — see [Hardware](docs/readme-details.en.md#hardware). ## Docs and contributing Contributions are welcome — start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Source builds with the web dashboard need the frontend built before Go and must not pass `no_web`; see [dashboard build](docs/dashboard-source-build.md). More: [Getting started](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) · [README details](docs/readme-details.en.md) · [A team from one CLI](docs/single-cli-team.en.md) · [bothouse in DSH](docs/platforms/dsh.en.md) · [Discord and Feishu setup](docs/connect-discord-feishu.md) · [Model and reasoning](docs/model-and-reasoning.md) · [Codex bot session isolation](docs/codex-session-isolation.md) · [Dispatcher and team memory](docs/ccm-and-wiki.md) · [Role packs](docs/persona-packs.md) · [Per-role Wiki and nightly reflection](bridge/contrib/wiki/README.md) · [Guardrails and tools](bridge/contrib/hooks/README.md) · [Memory read-frequency report](docs/READ_FREQUENCY.md) · [Cross-CLI workflow hooks](docs/workflow-hooks.md) · [Usage API](docs/api/usage.md) · [Self-hosted web protocol](bridge/docs/cloud-web.md) · [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [Lead collaboration scripts](bridge/contrib/lead/README.md) Most guides are currently in Chinese; the self-hosted web protocol is in English. ## Community Questions, ideas and the teams you build are all welcome. | Drop by | | | --- | --- | | [Discord](https://discord.gg/aJmcnrt5ZB) | chat with users and contributors | | [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/issues) | bugs and ideas | | [Pull requests](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/pulls) | build it with us | | [linux.do](https://linux.do) | Chinese community forum | ## License and thanks - **License:** [Apache-2.0](LICENSE); see [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md). Third-party dependencies are listed in [THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md](THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md). - **Thanks:** the bridge is built on [cc-connect](https://github.com/chenhg5/cc-connect) and keeps its full commit history, so the contributor list includes cc-connect's authors and contributors. Thanks to [@chenhg5](https://github.com/chenhg5) and every cc-connect contributor; the upstream MIT notice is kept in [bridge/LICENSE-MIT-upstream](bridge/LICENSE-MIT-upstream). - **Community:** [linux.do](https://linux.do) ## Star History The administrator [usage page](docs/api/usage.md) includes local member token rankings and per-member daily, role and model breakdowns.

decision.reason: The fixed package is named bothouse-pet but its bundle patch mounts dsh-pet, the upstream package identity, rather than its own exported native package. The retained MIT upstream license does not resolve this installation/source mapping conflict.

# bothouse-plugin-template 最小的 bothouse 插件：连上桥的角色事件，把绑定了本插件的角色的状态写进 DSH 日志。拿它当起点写自己的插件，做法见 [插件开发说明](../../docs/plugins/plugin-dev.md)。 配置（插件页 → 配置）： | 字段 | 说明 | | --- | --- | | `bridge` | 桥的管理 API 地址，默认 `http://127.0.0.1:9820` | | `token` | `config.toml` 里 `[management] token`，编辑器里显示为「已设置」 | | `statuses` | 只处理这些状态；空表示全部（idle working thinking celebrate error speech） | 只处理在 `/api/v1/plugins/role-bindings` 里把 `bothouse-plugin-template` 设为 `enabled: true` 的角色。
# bothouse **English** ｜ [中文](README.zh-CN.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/zuiho-kai/bothouse?style=flat-square&color=e8833a&label=release)](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-4a7c59?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS%20%C2%B7%20Windows%20%C2%B7%20Linux-555?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/releases) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/zuiho-kai/bothouse?style=flat-square&color=f2b33d)](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/stargazers) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join-5865F2?style=flat-square&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/aJmcnrt5ZB) **Put someone else's agent to work for you: a friend's Claude Code or Codex joins your group chat, and one @mention gets it started.** Bring your own AIs too: a team-lead AI splits the work and hands it out; they all share one memory. [Video](#video) · [Why](#why) · [Where to start](#usage) · [Install](#install) · [How it works](#how) · [Features](#features) · [Memory](#memory) · [Platforms](#platforms) · [Compare](#compare) · [Roadmap](#roadmap) · [Community](#community) · [Docs](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) · [Discord task forum](bridge/docs/task-forum.md)

**Watch it in 3 minutes** — one message goes in; the crew splits the work, does it and hands it back. Click the cover to play.

```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/main/install.sh | sh ``` ## Why I had Claude Code, Codex and DeepSeek open at once across two screens, and getting them to work together was a pain. So I put them all in one Discord group, let one of them hand out the work, and gave them a shared memory. No extra account, no extra subscription — you direct them from your computer, phone or browser. **The most common way people use it now: borrowing someone else's agents.** zzzx0757 in our group works this way every day with the author's (zuiho-kai) agents: he @mentions the lead AI in Discord, and the work goes out — the Codex role writes the code, the DeepSeek role polishes the copy — and the results come back to him. Your friend's Claude and Codex become staff on loan: no extra subscription just to generate images, no six people sharing one login. One computer stays on, and the whole group can hand out work. This repo is built the same way: I hand out work in the group, the agents each take a piece, one that wasn't involved reviews it, and then it gets merged. ## Where to start | What you have | Where to start | | --- | --- | | **A friend's agents** | Have a friend who runs bothouse invite you to their group, or bring their roles into yours. @mention one and it starts; nothing to install on your side. | | **Several AI command-line tools** | The setup wizard (see [Install](#install)): each role gets one of your signed-in AI command-line tools ("CLIs" below). | | **One model, one account** | Create several members on the same model, each with its own job. See [A team from one CLI](docs/single-cli-team.en.md). | | **DSH** (DeepSeek Harness, DeepSeek's own AI assistant app) | Say "install bothouse-dsh for me" in DSH, or run `bothouse module add dsh`. See [bothouse in DSH](docs/platforms/dsh.en.md). | ## Install Install with one command, then run `bothouse` to open the setup wizard in your browser: pick a platform, connect your bots, choose a local CLI for each role, and you are ready. ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/main/install.sh | sh ``` The Windows command, package downloads and the background service are in [Getting started](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md). On macOS, daemon install and restart allow a 30-second window for launchd to remove and reload the old job. If loading still fails, follow the error's recovery command; `bothouse daemon start` loads the saved service definition. **Let an AI agent install it for you:** give Claude Code, Codex or any agent CLI this repo link and say "install bothouse and connect it to Discord". The agent-side steps are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#用户说配-discord--飞书把这个配好接上-discord). ## How it works Only three ideas to learn: - **The team-lead AI** ("the lead" in the docs) — the AI you talk to in each chat channel. It splits real work and hands it out by skill and quota, so five AIs in one group still don't talk over each other. The others reply when you mention or name them. - **Workspaces** — big jobs (more than about ten minutes, or code changes and tests) go to a separate job channel with a handoff that carries your original words, the scope and what "done" looks like. Chat never stalls; one workspace, one job. The lead keeps a task board, and the bridge looks at every job every ten minutes. Results come back with proof, and only decisions that need you come back to chat. This is what we call **team mode**. - **Shared memory** — every role reads and writes the same Markdown notes, so whoever picks up a job already knows the background. See [Memory](#memory). Jobs can return results in batches: accepting a batch keeps the job and workspace open, while accepting the final report closes the job. Workspace agents use `ws-up --report --batch` for intermediate results and `--final` (the default) for the final handback; see the [workspace playbook](bridge/contrib/lead/PLAYBOOK.zh-CN.md). More detail — who replies when nobody is named, the nightly review, guardrails, switching the lead by hand — is in [How the team works](docs/readme-details.en.md#how-the-team-works). ## Features | You want | How bothouse helps | | --- | --- | | **Someone else's agent working for you** | A friend adds their Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and others to your group; you @mention one to hand it a job and the result comes back to you. As long as their computer is on, you can do it from your phone. | | **An AI team of your own** | Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, DSH, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Grok and more; each role has its own name, persona and session. | | **A team from one account** | Several members on one model, each with its own job; they hand work to each other by mention. | | **The chat apps you use** | Discord, Feishu, QQ or DSH; Discord and Feishu have phone apps, so you can hand out work from bed. | | **Long jobs stay on track** | Handoffs carry your original words; a second AI with a clean context checks the result; "fixed" needs evidence. | | **A nightly review** | Fixes and dedupes what was noted during the day; your repeated corrections become draft rules that apply only after you approve. | | **Manage it from your phone** | A web dashboard: who is busy, quota used, edit personas, add a note to running work. | Also: [team desk](docs/readme-details.en.md#team-desk) — a pixel office that shows the team at work; [remote pairing](docs/readme-details.en.md#remote-pairing) — run your team from another computer or your phone with a six-digit code; [per-channel model and reasoning](docs/model-and-reasoning.md); [role packs and avatars](docs/readme-details.en.md#roles-and-avatars); [optional image generation](docs/readme-details.en.md#image-generation).

Task board: what each workspace is doing and what landed today, at a glance.
Team desk: who is working on what, live; every light is a real event.

Roles: which CLI each role runs, what it is busy with, which model — pause or restart in one click.
Library: personas and avatars come in packs; pick one and it is ready to work.
_Top left: real channel footage. The rest: the author's own team desk and dashboard._ ### Characters (optional) Each role can also wear a persona and an avatar — handy if you want your team to have faces and personalities. The author's own team looks like this; pick from [role packs and avatars](docs/readme-details.en.md#roles-and-avatars), or skip it and keep the plain tools.

## Memory you can see The team's memory is a plain folder of Markdown files. Each incoming message first looks up the relevant pages; a nightly review fixes what was written down wrong. You can read and edit it directly; Git records every change and pushes it to your own private GitHub repo, so the memory follows you to another computer. - **Only the titles go in:** each turn picks the related memories by keyword and injects their titles and line numbers; a role opens the full text when it needs it. It costs very little and cuts rework — fewer "I already told you that". The idea came from vLLM. - **Light on cost:** no knowledge-graph CRUD and no always-on vector store, so cost and memory use stay small. - **Memory forum:** the panel's "Memory forum" page scores each memory as a reply — upvotes, downvotes, how often it was pushed and quoted — so a wrong memory falls down instead of being repeated. See [dispatcher and team memory](docs/ccm-and-wiki.md) (Chinese) and the [Wiki galaxy](docs/readme-details.en.md#wiki-galaxy). ## Platforms | Platform | Status | Capabilities | | --- | --- | --- | | Discord | Full support | Multiple roles, mentions, task handoffs, teammate status and log channels; slash commands in servers and DMs | | Feishu (Lark) | Single role | Conversation with one connected role | | QQ official bot | Manual setup | Group/private chat, group @user and @everyone; see [QQ Bot setup](bridge/docs/qqbot.md) | | DSH desktop app / web | Experimental | A Channels page inside the DeepSeek Harness desktop app (default) or DSH web; see [DSH](docs/platforms/dsh.en.md) | QQ via OneBot/NapCat, remote access from your phone with Tailscale, and hardware bodies for roles are in [Platform details](docs/readme-details.en.md#platform-details). ## bothouse and other projects **Most of them are one agent with a crew of sub-agents. bothouse puts the several AIs you already use into one group chat, splits the work between them, and gives them one shared memory.** **Which to pick**: for a personal assistant you can reach anywhere and that learns you, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent are mature; to watch several coding agents race side by side, pick Orca; if you only use DSH and want a few bots, there are Tobs and DS Bot. If you already have several AI CLIs and want them to split the work in one group and share one memory — say it before bed, collect results in the morning — pick bothouse. Many of these can be used together.
Side-by-side tables People often ask: DeepSeek now ships its own agent, and there are Tobs, DS Bot, OpenClaw and more — how is bothouse different? - **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** is DeepSeek's official open-source agent framework, still a developer preview: agent teams are experimental, and there's no built-in long-term memory unless you plug one in. bothouse's assignment, task board and shared memory are in daily use already — and DSH itself can join as one of the teammates. - **Tobs and DS Bot** are community bot projects built on DSH; every bot in the team runs on DSH. bothouse isn't tied to one agent: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and DSH each take their own jobs in the same group. | | What it is | Which AIs | How several AIs work together | Memory | Where you chat | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **bothouse** | **A coordination layer on your own computer + web panel** | **Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, DSH; Grok and more; OpenAI-compatible APIs** | **The lead role hands work to separate workspaces; task board; one thread per job** | **One shared Markdown wiki, reviewed nightly** | Discord, self-hosted web, Feishu, QQ, DSH web (experimental) | | [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) | DeepSeek's official agent framework (developer preview) | DeepSeek by default; other providers can be added | Subagents; agent teams are experimental | No built-in long-term memory; memory plugins can be added | Its own desktop app and web UI | | [Tobs](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot) | Bot plugin built on DSH | Models configured in DSH | @ whoever you need; assignments | One Git repo per bot | Feishu, Slack, Discord, QQ, WeChat | | [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot) | Desktop app / plugin / Docker built on DSH | Models configured in DSH | A chief bot runs the team; group admins coordinate | Memory per bot and per group | In the app | Mature personal assistants and coding tools get compared too: | | What it is | How several AIs work together | Memory | How bothouse differs | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) | Personal AI assistant with pluggable harnesses (Claude, Codex and more), 20+ chat apps | Team preset: a coordinator delegates to researcher, writer and reviewer | Sessions split per agent; Memory Wiki shared by default, can be split per agent | One assistant with swappable engines vs several signed-in CLIs working side by side in one group | | [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) | Self-improving personal assistant, any model | Isolated subagents in parallel | Manages its own memory, writes its own skills | It learns one person; bothouse gives a team one shared memory | | [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) | Multi-agent coding IDE using your own CLIs | Several agents race on one task; merge the best | Left to each CLI | It has you watch the race; bothouse lets you hand it off and walk away | | [LobeHub](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub) | Open-source agent workspace (web, desktop, mobile; cloud or self-hosted), 40+ model providers, can bring in Claude Code and Codex | Agent Team: sequential, parallel, iterative or debate; delegated tasks | Structured memories you can review and edit | A full workspace you move into vs a small program that drives your signed-in CLIs in the group you already use, with one Git-tracked Markdown memory | Others people ask about: | | What it's good at | What bothouse adds | | --- | --- | --- | | [Raft](https://www.testingcatalog.com/raft-1-0-puts-ai-agents-in-team-mode/) | People and agents in one new Slack-like workspace | No new app: plugs into the Discord, Feishu or web you already use; open source and self-hostable | | [Cindy](https://github.com/makecindy/cindy) | One client for Claude Code and Codex; switch models without losing context | The lead role splits the work and hands it out, so you don't have to | | [Tencent Mavis](https://technode.com/2026/05/21/tencent-unveils-mavis-ai-assistant-that-turns-pcs-into-conversational-interfaces/) | System-level assistant: files, PC and phone apps | Several AIs split project work: code, research, review | | [magpie](https://github.com/yetone/magpie) / [cc-switch](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch) | One place to manage model providers | Different layer: they decide which model, bothouse decides who takes which job and what the team remembers — use them together | | [llm-wiki](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/llm-wiki) | Turns sessions into a layered wiki memory | bothouse's memory builds on it and shares it across roles |
## Roadmap - **Share across people:** bring every teammate's Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and DeepSeek into one group, so one person tunes the AI and the whole team uses it — shared lessons from the nightly review, and each person's own standards and habits remembered separately. (Splitting work inside one group already works — see [How it works](#how).) - **Claim before starting:** lock assignments so two members never start the same task. - **Specialists on demand:** "publish to the App Store" spins up a specialist that reads prior decisions, does the job and exits. - **Role packs and a plugin marketplace:** personas, memory templates and tools in one-step bundles; browse community roles. - **Portable memory and semantic search:** carry the Wiki between computers and models, with semantic retrieval beside keyword search. - **Automatic workspace cleanup:** clear context after the last assignment so the next task starts fresh. - **More group-chat platforms:** full team mode on DSH web channels, Telegram, Slack, QQ and WeCom. - **Team-wide rules and skills:** push the team's rules, skills and tool settings to every member's computer in one step. - **Deep support for popular DSH plugins:** reuse the DSH plugin ecosystem, with deep support for the popular plugins. - **Hardware:** give a role a small ESP32 round-screen body with [bothouse-iot](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse-iot) — see [Hardware](docs/readme-details.en.md#hardware). ## Docs and contributing Contributions are welcome — start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Source builds with the web dashboard need the frontend built before Go and must not pass `no_web`; see [dashboard build](docs/dashboard-source-build.md). More: [Getting started](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) · [README details](docs/readme-details.en.md) · [A team from one CLI](docs/single-cli-team.en.md) · [bothouse in DSH](docs/platforms/dsh.en.md) · [Discord and Feishu setup](docs/connect-discord-feishu.md) · [Model and reasoning](docs/model-and-reasoning.md) · [Codex bot session isolation](docs/codex-session-isolation.md) · [Dispatcher and team memory](docs/ccm-and-wiki.md) · [Role packs](docs/persona-packs.md) · [Per-role Wiki and nightly reflection](bridge/contrib/wiki/README.md) · [Guardrails and tools](bridge/contrib/hooks/README.md) · [Memory read-frequency report](docs/READ_FREQUENCY.md) · [Cross-CLI workflow hooks](docs/workflow-hooks.md) · [Usage API](docs/api/usage.md) · [Self-hosted web protocol](bridge/docs/cloud-web.md) · [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [Lead collaboration scripts](bridge/contrib/lead/README.md) Most guides are currently in Chinese; the self-hosted web protocol is in English. ## Community Questions, ideas and the teams you build are all welcome. | Drop by | | | --- | --- | | [Discord](https://discord.gg/aJmcnrt5ZB) | chat with users and contributors | | [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/issues) | bugs and ideas | | [Pull requests](https://github.com/zuiho-kai/bothouse/pulls) | build it with us | | [linux.do](https://linux.do) | Chinese community forum | ## License and thanks - **License:** [Apache-2.0](LICENSE); see [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md). Third-party dependencies are listed in [THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md](THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md). - **Thanks:** the bridge is built on [cc-connect](https://github.com/chenhg5/cc-connect) and keeps its full commit history, so the contributor list includes cc-connect's authors and contributors. Thanks to [@chenhg5](https://github.com/chenhg5) and every cc-connect contributor; the upstream MIT notice is kept in [bridge/LICENSE-MIT-upstream](bridge/LICENSE-MIT-upstream). - **Community:** [linux.do](https://linux.do) ## Star History The administrator [usage page](docs/api/usage.md) includes local member token rankings and per-member daily, role and model breakdowns.

dsh-purge — DeepSeek Harness 本地运行时适配插件

适配版 v1.1.76 · 对应 dsh 0.2.2-rc.5

中文 | English

> 本包是 `dsh-purge` 的**兼容性适配重建版**，用于给自己电脑上已安装的官方 DeepSeek Harness 做本地配置与产物层适配。原仓库与其 npm 包均已下线，因此**按包名安装（`dsh plugin add dsh-purge`）不可用**，请按本文第四节的 tarball / 本地目录 / 手动三种方式安装。 > > 本版本针对 **dsh 0.2.2-rc.5** 重新校准了补丁锚点与运行期接口，适配细节见 [ADAPTATION-NOTES.md](ADAPTATION-NOTES.md)。 > > 要在**另一台电脑**上装：直接看 [INSTALL-OTHER-PC.md](INSTALL-OTHER-PC.md)（拷贝 zip → 解压到英文路径 → 跑 `install.ps1`）。 --- ## 目录 - [一、这是什么](#一这是什么) - [二、能力总览](#二能力总览) - [三、环境要求](#三环境要求) - [四、安装](#四安装) - [五、目录结构与运行时文件](#五目录结构与运行时文件) - [六、使用](#六使用) - [七、配置项](#七配置项) - [八、工作方式](#八工作方式) - [九、更新、还原、卸载](#九更新还原卸载) - [十、常见问题（FAQ）](#十常见问题faq) - [十一、兼容性](#十一兼容性) - [十二、署名与许可](#十二署名与许可) --- ## 一、这是什么 `dsh-purge` 是给**本机已安装的官方 DeepSeek Harness** 使用的一个插件。它不加载模型权重、不修改 Harness 源码树，只在**宿主层**做两类事情： 1. **统一本地默认值**。Harness 的许多行为由若干默认常量与默认策略决定（提示词段落措辞、审批策略默认值、沙箱模式默认值、工具描述文本、交付物卡片行为等）。这些值在官方包里是写死的；本插件用一张**可回滚的补丁表**把它们在你本机改成同一套统一取值，行为一致、可随时还原。 2. **集中查看与维护**。侧栏面板按组列出每个条目的状态（`applied` / `pending` / `skipped` / `missing_file`），支持一键应用、还原、卸载，以及提示词段与规则集的编辑。 | 你会得到 | 说明 | |---|---| | **侧栏面板** | 会话标题旁的按钮，右侧栏两页：**适配** / **演练台（可选模块）** | | **适配页** | 分组显示补丁状态；应用 / 还原 / 卸载；提示词编辑；多套规则集 | | **演练台** | 本机资产与技能清点页，首次进入需确认授权声明；不使用可以完全不进 | | **宿主默认值** | 提示词段、权限策略、工具上限、卡片行为统一取值；官方能力保留 | | **启动自检** | 可选开启；npm/pnpm 重装覆盖 `node_modules` 后不必手改文件 | 支持官方 **Web（`dsh web`）** 与官方**桌面 EXE**；两个宿主是两份独立的 `$DSH_HOME`，**分别安装、分别应用**。 路径探测顺序：`$DSH_HOME` → dsh 启动器旁的 `.dsh` → `~/.dsh`。不改 Harness 源码树，只改本机 `@deepseek-ai/*` 包产物与用户目录下的覆盖文件。 --- ## 二、能力总览 - **补丁表**：按组列出每项状态，重复应用幂等；原文对不上的条目只显示 `skipped`，不会乱改。 - **提示词段**：默认使用插件内**加密内置**的那份；也可编辑器里的 `$DSH_HOME/prompt-inject.md` 覆盖。 - **规则集**：多套 `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`，启用即写入 `$DSH_HOME`，删除只从列表移除。 - **Skill**：导入压缩包或文件夹到当前宿主的 `$DSH_HOME/skills//SKILL.md`，由 DSH 自己加载；卸载插件不删你的 Skill。 - **本机地址清单**：面板里逐行登记设备 IP 或完整主机名，写入 `$DSH_HOME/net-scope-allow.txt`（仅记录用途，用于本地资产清点）。 - **回退**：输入框旁「回退一次 / 回退上一轮」，已发送内容回到输入框，可从当前这一轮重来；聊天里 `/rewind` 等价。 - **自动重试 / 续跑**：`autoRetry` 失败重试、`autoContinue` 自动续跑，次数可配。 --- ## 三、环境要求 | 项 | 要求 | |---|---| | dsh | **0.2.2-rc.5**（本包 `dshTarget`）；0.2.0 / 0.2.1 / 0.2.2-rc.1~rc.4 亦可用，个别条目会显示 `skipped` | | 宿主 | 官方桌面 EXE（profile `desktop`）或官方 `dsh web`（profile `web`） | | Node.js | **≥ 18**；Windows 下要「无闪窗」需要 **≥ 22** | | 包管理器 | 用 dsh 自带的 pnpm（`dsh plugin` 会调用它），不必单独装 | | 网络 | 本包已适配本地目录安装，**不需要联网**即可完成安装 | --- ## 四、安装 ### 4.0 先确认装到哪个宿主 | 你在跑 | profile | 说明 | |---|---|---| | 官方桌面 EXE | `desktop` | profile 需**先启动过一次客户端**才生成；安装前**完全退出**（托盘右键退出） | | 官方 `dsh web` | `web` | 安装前停掉正在跑的 `dsh web` | 确认 `$DSH_HOME` 是你实际在用的那一份（本机常有两份 `.dsh`）： ```powershell $cands = @() if ($env:DSH_HOME) { $cands += $env:DSH_HOME } $cands += "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh" $cands += @("$env:APPDATA\DeepSeek Harness\dsh-home", "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\DeepSeek Harness\dsh-home") $cands | Select-Object -Unique | Where-Object { $_ -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $_ "profiles")) } ``` ```sh # macOS / Linux ls -d "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}"/profiles 2>/dev/null ``` 进入 `profiles//package.json`，`"name"` 应为 `dsh-profile-web` 或 `dsh-profile-desktop`。 --- ### 4.1 方式 A：本地目录安装（推荐，离线可用） 把本目录（能看到 `package.json` 的那一层）直接当包源： > 先放到**纯英文路径**再装（例如 `D:\dsh-plugins\dsh-purge-0.2.2`）。`dsh plugin` 底层调用 pnpm，路径含中文时可能报 `ERR_PNPM_STORE_DIR_OPEN_OPERATION_LOCK`；`install.ps1` 会自动把插件与 pnpm store 都切到 ASCII 目录来规避。 ```powershell # Web 宿主 dsh plugin --profile web add D:\dsh-plugins\dsh-purge-0.2.2 # 桌面宿主（先完全退出桌面客户端） dsh plugin --profile desktop add D:\dsh-plugins\dsh-purge-0.2.2 ``` ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-purge-0.2.2 ``` 当前 shell 就在目录里时也可以 `dsh plugin --profile web add .`。 拷目录要拷**整个目录**（`lib/ client.js docs/ presets/ skills/ bin/`），不要只拷几个 `.js` —— `client.js` 是侧栏前端产物，缺了就只有命令行、没有面板。 --- ### 4.2 方式 B：手动安装（CLI 不可用时兜底） 只改**正在用的那个宿主**对应的 profile，不要动另一个，也不要删原有 bundle。 **第 1 步：把插件放进 `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-purge`** 目录名必须是 `dsh-purge`，里面 `package.json` 的 `"name"` 也必须是 `dsh-purge`。把本目录整体复制并改名即可。 **第 2 步：备份并修改 profile 的 `package.json`** Web → `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/package.json`；桌面 → `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop/package.json`。**只追加两处**： 1. `dependencies` 增加 `"dsh-purge": "file:../../plugins/dsh-purge"` 2. `dsh.profile.bundles` **末尾**追加 `"dsh-purge"`（已有就别重复加） ```json { "name": "dsh-profile-web", "private": true, "dependencies": { "dsh-purge": "file:../../plugins/dsh-purge" }, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ "@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-purge" ] } } } ``` JSON 必须合法（新增项前有逗号、最后一项后没有多余逗号）。`file:` 保持相对路径；`patchReload`、其它插件、版本号都别动。 **第 3 步：只在刚改的那个 profile 目录里装依赖** ```sh cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/web" # 或 profiles/desktop pnpm install ``` 成功标志：出现 `profiles//node_modules/dsh-purge/package.json`。报 `Could not resolve` 就查 `file:` 路径；JSON 解析失败就修逗号或还原备份。 --- ### 4.3 一键脚本（Windows） 本目录自带 `install.ps1`，会自动定位宿主、备份 profile、安装依赖并打印补丁状态： ```powershell # 桌面宿主 powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1 -Profile desktop # Web 宿主 powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1 -Profile web -DshHome "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh" ``` 只查看状态、不做改动： ```powershell powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1 -Profile desktop -StatusOnly ``` 装前/装后想先做一次完整体检（**只读，不改任何文件**）： ```powershell powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\check.ps1 -Profile desktop ``` 它会检查 Node 版本、dsh CLI、`DSH_HOME` 候选、profile 是否初始化、路径是否纯英文、是否已装过、以及补丁状态汇总，最后一行给出 `RESULT: ready.` 或阻塞项。 --- ### 4.4 `dsh` 不在 PATH 怎么办 桌面版自带一份 CLI，Windows 通常在安装目录下： ``` <安装目录>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd ``` 直接用它，参数完全一致： ```powershell & "D:\dsh\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd" plugin --profile desktop add D:\path\to\dsh-purge-0.2.2 ``` 先 `Get-Command dsh` 看一眼有没有；没有就用上面的绝对路径。 --- ### 4.5 安装后的三步 1. **完全退出并重开**你装的那个宿主：桌面端托盘退出再开；`dsh web` 停进程再启动。 2. 在**那个宿主**上点会话标题旁的 **dsh-purge** → **适配** → **应用**（不在设置页里）。 3. 应用成功后宿主会自重启一次（补丁在重启后加载）；没跑完不会重启。 > Web 的开关只影响 Web，桌面的开关只影响桌面。不要在一个宿主里给另一个宿主点应用。 > 也可以纯命令行应用：`node <插件目录>\bin\dsh-purge.js --apply`。 --- ### 4.6 安装验证清单 - [ ] `profiles//package.json` 里同时有 `dependencies.dsh-purge` 和 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里的 `dsh-purge` - [ ] `profiles//node_modules/dsh-purge/package.json` 存在 - [ ] 宿主界面会话标题旁出现 **dsh-purge** 按钮，右侧栏能打开 - [ ] 聊天里 `/purge status` 打印 `DSH_HOME` 与补丁列表，且路径是你实际在跑的那份 - [ ] 模型侧有 `purge_status` / `purge_apply` / `purge_revert` 三个工具（说明 bundle 已加载） - [ ] `node <插件>\bin\dsh-purge.js --status` 能列出补丁状态 可选包（例如第三方 mnemon / liangshen 相关条目）没装时显示 `skipped` / `missing_file`，不阻塞应用，属正常。 --- ## 五、目录结构与运行时文件 包内： | 路径 | 说明 | |---|---| | `bin/dsh-purge.js` | CLI 入口（`--status / --apply / --revert / --uninstall / --edit`） | | `lib/` | 补丁引擎、路径探测、shim 写入、更新、卸载、演练台（`lib/redteam/`） | | `lib/core.js` | 补丁表与匹配引擎（本适配版的主要改动都在这里） | | `lib/asset-table.js` | 内置加密提示词（由 `scripts/embed-default-prompt.mjs` 生成） | | `client.js` | 侧栏前端产物（构建自 `scripts/build-client.mjs`） | | `cordis.patch.yml` | bundle patch：注册 `dsh-purge`、`dsh-purge/redteam`、`store`、`ui` 四个入口 | | `presets/` / `skills/` | 预设与随包技能（可选模块用） | | `scripts/` | 构建 / 嵌入 / 补丁脚本 | 运行时（`$DSH_HOME` 下，Web 与桌面各一份）： | 文件/目录 | 说明 | |---|---| | `prompt-inject.md` | 会话覆盖段；用户文件，还原时保留 | | `rules/` | 规则集（`AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`） | | `skills//SKILL.md` | 导入的技能 | | `net-scope-allow.txt` | 本机设备地址清单 | | `redteam/` | 演练台事实库（SQLite，可选模块） | | `dsh-purge/` | 插件状态：`applied.json`、`override-state.json`、`installed-rev` 等 | --- ## 六、使用 ```sh # 命令行 dsh-purge --status # 宿主、DSH_HOME、补丁 applied/pending、shim、备份 dsh-purge --apply # 应用全部补丁（提示词段 + 代码默认值 + shim + override） dsh-purge --revert # 回滚还原 dsh-purge --uninstall # 卸载（已应用则先还原） dsh-purge --edit # 编辑注入文件 prompt-inject.md dsh-purge --help # 聊天命令 /purge status | apply | revert | uninstall | edit | help /rules list | use | create | delete | reset | help /skills list | import <压缩包或文件夹> | create [说明] | delete | help /rewind # 模型工具 purge_status purge_apply purge_revert ``` 面板：**适配** 页从上到下是补丁状态、提示词、本机地址清单、规则集、Skill；**演练台** 页首次进入需确认声明（读声明 → 等倒计时 → 滚到文末 → 勾三项）。 --- ## 七、配置项 改 `$DSH_HOME/profiles//cordis.patch.yml` 里的 `dsh-purge` 条目，**重启宿主**生效： ```yaml - insert: - id: dsh-purge name: 'dsh-purge' inject: [systemPrompt, tools] config: enabled: true # 插件总开关 autoApplyOnStart: false # 启动时自动应用（默认关） autoUpdateOnStart: false # 启动时检查更新 autoRevertOnMissing: false # 保留字段 injectOnce: false # 保留字段 stripMnemon: true # 去掉 mnemon 段 verbose: false # 控制台详细日志 postPrompt: "" # 额外提示段（默认空） postPromptOrder: 5100 # 需大于内置全局顺序，否则该段被跳过 autoRetry: true # 失败自动重试 retryMax: 3 autoContinue: false # 自动续跑 continueMax: 3 continueText: "继续" capabilityProtocol: true # 注入能力协议段 hooksDenyBypass: true - id: dsh-purge-redteam name: dsh-purge/redteam - id: dsh-purge-redteam-store name: dsh-purge/redteam/store config: root: !!js dshHomePath('redteam') - id: dsh-purge-redteam-ui name: dsh-purge/redteam/ui ``` profile 层的 `cordis.patch.yml`（用户 patch 层）在内置配置之后加载，后续应用插件会保留你的 `insert`。 --- ## 八、工作方式 ```mermaid flowchart TD A["启动或点应用"] --> B{"条目已生效?"} B -->|是| C["跳过（幂等）"] B -->|否| D["目标文件备份为 <文件>.dshpurge.bak"] D --> E["按补丁表替换对应文件"] E --> F["写入 shim（dsh.cmd / dsh.ps1 / dsh）"] F --> G["挂载插件内置提示词段"] ``` 提示词段来源优先级：`prompt-inject.md`（非空）→ 当前目录被勾选且非空的本地 md → 插件内置默认值；再由 workspace baseline 策略（`strict` / `fallback` / `always`）决定是否保留 DSH 的 baseline 段。Skill **不进**注入段，也不顶替提示词。 补丁匹配是**纯文本锚点**：锚点对不上（上游改了写法）就判 `skipped` 并保持原样，不会产生半改文件；本适配版已按 dsh 0.2.2-rc.5 的实际产物逐条校准（见 [ADAPTATION-NOTES.md](ADAPTATION-NOTES.md)）。 --- ## 九、更新、还原、卸载 **还原**（保留插件，只回原版宿主）： ```sh dsh-purge --revert # 或 /purge revert，或面板「还原」 ``` - 每个目标文件应用前备份为 `<文件>.dshpurge.bak`；还原用备份覆盖回去并删除备份；没有备份时只去掉 shim 里由本插件写入的行。 - `prompt-inject.md` 是用户文件，还原时保留。 **卸载**： ```sh dsh-purge --uninstall # 或 /purge uninstall，或面板「适配 → 卸载」 ``` 会先还原（若已应用）再删除注入文件、规则库与插件登记，然后重启宿主。 **升级到新版**：用新目录替换旧目录后重跑安装（方式 A / B），再应用一次。npm/pnpm 覆盖 `node_modules` 后补丁会丢，把 `autoApplyOnStart` 设成 `true` 可自动补回。 --- ## 十、常见问题（FAQ） **1. `dsh plugin add dsh-purge` 装不上** 原 npm 包已下线。请用 [4.1](#41-方式-a本地目录安装推荐离线可用) 的本地目录方式，或 [4.2](#42-方式-b手动安装cli-不可用时兜底) 手动方式。 **2. `dsh plugin` 报 `pnpm was not found`** 用 dsh 自带 CLI（`resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd`），它会带内置 pnpm；自己装的话确保 pnpm 在 PATH。 **3. 报 `plugin command failed`** 看它给出的 `logPath`。常见是 profile JSON 写坏、`file:` 路径不对。 **4. 报版本不匹配（incompatible）** 本包 `dshTarget` 是 `0.2.2-rc.5`。确认 dsh 在 0.2.x；跨小版本可用： ```sh dsh plugin --profile web allow-version dsh-purge@1.1.76 --dsh-version <你的精确版本> --accept-risk ``` **5. 桌面端 `dsh plugin --profile desktop ...` 直接报错** 桌面 profile 还没初始化：先启动一次桌面客户端，**完全退出**后再跑命令。 **6. 装好了但会话标题旁没有 dsh-purge** - 装错宿主了（见 [4.0](#40-先确认装到哪个宿主)）； - 没重启宿主； - profile 里少了 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里的 `dsh-purge`（只加依赖不会加载）； - `client.js` 没跟着拷过去。 **7. 点了「应用」但行为没变** 补丁要**重启后**才加载。正确顺序：应用 → 等自动重启 → 新开一轮对话。 **8. 状态里出现 `skipped` / `missing_file`** 宿主版本不同或装了精简产物，锚点对不上时只显示跳过（不会乱改）。缺失项对应的可选包（第三方 mnemon / liangshen 等）没装时属正常，其余仍能完成。 **9. 想在另一台电脑上用** 可以。插件只与本机 `@deepseek-ai` 包和 `$DSH_HOME` 交互：把本目录整个拷过去，按第四节装一遍即可（无需联网）。 --- ## 十一、兼容性 | 插件版本 | 适配 dsh | 说明 | |---|---|---| | **1.1.76**（本适配版） | **0.2.2-rc.5** | 适配 rc.5 全部 332 包 + `pi-ai@1.6`；补齐红队预设/子代理接口/`CONTENT_REFUSED`，恢复 `#32` `#56` `#77` `#57` | | 1.1.76 同版向下 | 0.2.2-rc.1~rc.4、0.2.1-rc.x、0.2.0-rc.2 | 状态探测 **0 回归**，旧写法锚点与 `listChildren` 回退均保留 | | 1.1.75 | 0.2.2-rc.3 | 修复 `{{cwd}}` 变量缺失、组装兜底丢工具与 DSML 正文重试 | | 1.1.73–1.1.74 | 0.2.2-rc.3 | 锚点重校准 + 读前校验与 hooks 幂等修复 | | 1.1.71（上游镜像） | 0.2.0-rc.2 | 原仓库镜像版，0.2.2 上有 6 条锚点失效 | 未命中项在面板里显示 `skipped`，只影响那一条，不会产生半改文件。在 0.2.2 上应用后常态 `skipped` 仅剩 `#40`（0.1.5 专用兼容项）与 `#80`（旧版极简工具表回退项）。 不适配的条目不会被盲改，只会 `pending` / `skipped`。 --- ## 十二、署名与许可 本项目为 MIT 开源。署名要求沿用原作者条款：借用名称、思路、代码或提示词须署名并写明来源。原始来源：**`YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge`（作者：小杨）**；镜像重建：**`ZXEB/dsh-purge`**；本目录为适配重建。 使用范围：本插件只作用于**你自己电脑上已安装的 Harness**（本机 `@deepseek-ai` 包、本地 profile 与 `$DSH_HOME`），以及你有权管理的环境。请勿将其用于他人的设备、账号或信息系统。 本项目按 MIT「现状」提供，不担保完整性与适用性；部署、运行、修改、分发及其产生的一切结果由使用者自行承担。 **许可**：MIT，见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)（版权行保留原作者 `Copyright (c) 2026 小杨`）。

structuralOverrides.reason: The fixed root is a private repository/discovery wrapper with no main or exports; its patch names a separate dsh-go-plugin-screen package. Installable screen/plugin manifests are considered separately. It is not itself an independent native plugin.

The fixed manifest explicitly labels this release [DEMO], and the README calls its release a Demo console for DaVinci Resolve. It is retained as an explicit demonstration outcome, not promoted as a regular catalog entry; native code and MCP/Python/model-download capabilities are recorded without execution.

The same-commit patch only configures the official @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai provider. It requires a separately started tools/numes-free-failover.mjs proxy; it does not mount its own native Cordis plugin. A dsh.bundle.patch field alone does not make this provider configuration a native plugin.

The fixed package is named bothouse-pet but its bundle patch mounts dsh-pet, the upstream package identity, rather than its own exported native package. The retained MIT upstream license does not resolve this installation/source mapping conflict.
